classes.printed_name: Predator (Dr. Razno) -- may be Guise or Innate

class_skills.summary: Action: destroy a pair of Motes for one cumulative benefit — Immunity to a chosen status; attacks/spells of a chosen damage type ignore Resistances; or Resistance to a chosen type. Up to (SL) benefits active, no repeats.
Begin a conflict scene with (SL × 2) Motes, up to your limit. Triggers on the Turn when swapping in mid-conflict.
Action: release Motes toward up to three creatures, 2 MP per Mote. Each delivered Mote restores (SL × 5) HP or MP, your choice. Released Motes are destroyed.

Action: release any number of Motes as a ranged (DEX + WLP) attack, 2 MP each. Each target loses (SL × 4) HP or MP per Mote — HP against Defense, MP against Magic Defense. Ignores Resistances. Motes are destroyed hit or miss.
Reaction: release Motes (2 MP each) to reduce incoming damage to you or up to three creatures — each Mote reduces the damage by (SL × 2), before Affinities.

When a GM-imposed Clock resolves in your favour during a conflict scene, recover (SL × 5) MP — turning back the Miasma Clock counts. And +(SL ÷ 2) to Checks on the Objective action or when supporting a Group Check toward an Objective.
Action + 1 Fabula Point: produce any Lucky Treasure you can describe from your supplies. It is gone at the end of the scene — describe why.

When a travel roll results in a Discovery — on the world map or in a dungeon — find a Lucky Treasure worth up to (level × 10 × SL) zenit, GM-determined. And you may spend Opportunities on a critical success to gain (SL × 50) zenit.
All damage you suffer outside a conflict scene that is not from an Attack or Spell — travel dangers, ritual Catastrophes, harmful terrain or weather — is reduced by (SL × 3).
Choose (SL) damage types when you take the Skill — fixed for the character's life. Action: spend up to (SL × 10) MP; every 10 MP applies Affliction of one chosen type to a creature you can see.
Action: spend 5 MP per target to grant Regeneration to up to (SL) creatures you can see.
Free action on your turn, 1 IP: remove (SL) status conditions from one creature you can see, and lock each removed condition out for the rest of the conflict scene.
Action: a second creature you can see suffers one status condition the target is already suffering. A copied Affliction carries every damage type of the original.
Action: one Afflicted target immediately takes 10 damage per type in its Affliction, or any number of Regenerating creatures immediately recover 10 HP. Neither consumes the condition.

Bind Arcana to your soul as the story grants them. Action + 30 MP summons a bound Arcanum and merges you with it — merge benefits, a pulse, and a dismiss effect. Taken at creation, you begin play with one Arcanum bound.
After you willingly dismiss a merged Arcanum, if you are in Crisis: you and every ally present recover (SL × 5) HP.
While merged: +(SL) damage on free attacks, pulses and spells. With an arcane, dagger or flail weapon equipped, your pulse and dismiss damage may ignore Affinities.

When summoning on your turn, choose up to two: reduce the MP cost by (SL × 5); and/or perform the pulse immediately. One option locks the Arcanum in until your next turn; both forfeit its dismiss effect for this summoning.
On a Result of 13+ on a Check to investigate a creature, item or location (Study included): bank up to (SL) questions about it, asked now or later, answered truthfully by the GM. Once per subject.
Permanently +(SL × 3) max MP, and +(SL) to Open Checks using (INS + INS).
Accuracy Checks may replace one Attribute die with Insight.
Start of conflict: spend up to (SL × 5) MP; every 5 MP reveals one Trait, or one named damage type's Affinity, of a creature you can see. Pressure points count as Traits for this Skill.
Perfect recall of any scene visited within the past week — revisit it in your mind and investigate it again, Flash of Insight included.
You may initiate Projects (the Archivist is a project-granting class; this is the class-skill route to Project access). When you initiate a Project, its initial cost is reduced by (SL × 50) zenit.

At session start, roll your INS die (SL) times and bank the results; when another creature you can see performs a Check, replace one of its dice with an unused banked value. Extra dice cost 500z, or no armour/shields this session, or erasing one emotion from a Bond — each option once.

Action: perform the Equipment action and spend up to (SL × 5) MP; each 5 MP buys one option, once each: swap Hunter Weapons with one ally you can see; a free attack with a weapon equipped this turn, High Roll 0; or reduce the next damage you suffer before your next turn by (SL), before Affinities.
When an ally causes creatures to lose HP, mark one of them until the next such trigger. Your attacks, spells and Skills deal (SL) extra damage to marked creatures.

After a creature you hold a Bond of admiration toward suffers status effects, spend 1 Fabula Point: they recover from any you choose that you are not also suffering — and you suffer them instead. When a Bond-of-inferiority creature rolls a fumble, recover from one status effect.
When you Guard and provide cover: recover (SL × 5) HP or MP, and until your next turn you may take any amount of the covered target's damage instead, up to (SL × 10) total.

When you Guard and provide cover, the covered creature chooses one before the end of their next turn: their next melee attack may strike creatures melee cannot normally reach, or their next attack or spell deals (SL × 2) extra damage.
A successful Support Check grants the leader +(SL) instead of the normal +1. ✎ The printed self-Resistance clause is removed.
Once per turn (anyone's turn), after you damage one or more enemies you have a Bond towards: recover (SL × 2) HP and (SL × 2) MP.
While in Crisis, Resistance to dark and poison.
Once per scene, when you enter Crisis: create a Bond of hatred towards a creature you can see that you have no Bond towards.
After another creature costs you HP by any means: Study them for free, with +(SL) to the Check.
Action: roll your Might die and lose that many HP. If you are not at 0, perform a free attack dealing +(SL + the roll) damage — all of it dark, and the type cannot change.
You know the direction and general distance to each character you have a Bond toward, and gain +(SL) to Checks to gather information about them or close the distance.
Strengthening an existing Bond gives your next Check a bonus equal to its new strength. You may also hold up to (SL) extra Bonds, and your Bonds may carry a fourth emotion — comfort or tension.

Adds a Bounty to your sheet — anything you are hunting: an NPC, a place, an artifact. Spend 1 Fabula Point to invoke it as a Trait (reroll) or as a Bond with strength (1 + Bounty Hunter level ÷ 5). Re-point it on level-up, on a rest, or with an Opportunity.

The core: 28 tools costing 2–4 IP each; gain two per Skill Level. Inventory action + the tool's IP applies its effect to a target you can see — no Check, and option-choosing tools are fixed when created. Tool damage on your Bounty ignores Resistances. New tools may be invented and bought (~1000z).
When you apply a "one creature" tool, spend up to (SL) extra IP; each IP adds one more creature you can see. Every target takes the full effect — 20 each, not 20 split.
After a conflict ends, if you did not Surrender: recover (SL + 1) Inventory Points — 2 more if you invoked your Bounty at least once during it.

At the start of a conflict scene, perform the Inventory action to produce an elemental shard, potion or tool of total IP cost (SL + 2) or lower — you still pay the IP. Triggers on the Turn when swapping in mid-conflict. Never in the same conflict as the Rogue's High Speed (the Telumorian Vambrace lifts the lock).

When a permitted-Species creature you can see falls to 0 HP, spend a quarter of your max HP: the GM reveals its abilities and you install one as an implant. Up to (SL) implants, at most three internal; your prosthetic implants deal (SL × 2) extra damage, capped at 6.

Action: (DEX + MIG) Check (+SL) against an NPC's Defense. On a success the GM reveals its attacks, actions and special rules; you choose one and the creature loses it until the end of the scene. Once per creature per scene.

When you or an ally spends or loses HP to one of your Skills or spells, reduce the amount by (SL × 2), to a minimum of half — then they shake one status effect or end one Scene-duration spell on them. Also +(SL) to butchering, surgery and wound-treatment Checks (never against Defense or Magic Defense).
After you damage an enemy in Crisis, regain 1 IP — up to (SL + 1) per scene.
When you spend or lose HP to one of your Skills or spells, one ally you can see recovers half that amount.

Action: free attack with an equipped weapon, High Roll 0. After it resolves, choose one: an ally who can hear you recovers (5 + SL × 5) HP, or use Bishop's Edict, Charging Cavalry or King's Castle for free (still paying its MP).
Action + 10 MP, until your next turn, choose one: all MP costs are doubled, or all sources of damage deal (SL × 3) extra. "All" means everyone on the battlefield — allies, enemies and you.
Action + 10 MP: one ally who can hear you performs a free attack (a basic attack if an NPC) at +(SL) Accuracy, High Roll 0. Works on allied NPCs.
Action + 10 MP, until your next turn, choose one: no creature can recover HP or MP, or all MP-restoring effects restore (SL × 5) more. The lockout is total and includes your own side.

After using Bishop's Edict, Charging Cavalry or King's Castle, choose a Player Character who can hear you and has not yet acted this round: they take their turn immediately after yours. Grants nobody an extra turn — it decides whose comes next.

The deck engine: grants the deck, the hand and the discard pile. In a conflict, action + up to (10 + SL × 5) MP (minimum 10): discard and resolve one card per 5 MP spent, maximum five — the set — then draw that many back.
Declared before a Check: until it ends, dice showing even numbers count doubled and other dice count 1..

When you resolve a set: with a joker and/or 7, +(SL) damage until your next turn; with a joker and/or 1, damage you suffer is reduced by (SL) before Affinities; with none of those, recover (SL × 2) HP immediately. A joker satisfying two rows is the player's choice.
When you hit one or more enemies with an attack on your turn, discard up to (SL + 1) cards and draw that many.

After an enemy resolves an Attack, Objective, Skill or Spell action, discard up to (SL + 1) cards that are jokers or match the action's suit (Attack ice, Objective fire, Skill earth, Spell air), draw back, then perform the Spell action for free, casting a spell of (SL × 5) MP or less — you still pay the MP. Once per round.
Each level grants one Entourage Member, chosen from the class roster.
With an arcane weapon equipped, when you cast a spell targeting allies, each may also recover up to (SL × your Bonds) MP. The Bond multiplier is capped at 3.

After resting where you can reach a crowd — in person or through technology or magic — gain (SL + 1) Reputation Points, holding at most (SL + 3); start with 2 if taken at creation. In a non-conflict scene, spend 2 on meeting an NPC: they have heard of you, positively or negatively inclined — your choice which.

Action + 1 Reputation Point: Opposed (WLP + WLP) against a nearby soldier-rank humanoid you can see. Success: control it until scene's end — one at a time, released at will, and released the moment you or an ally harms it.
Build disguises that hide your identity for short stretches. An in-person interaction running past a minute forces an Opposed (INS + WLP + SL) Check — lose and your identity is revealed.

Action, once per turn: spend MP to sing a verse — a volume (low 10 MP: one creature who can hear you; medium 20: every ally who can hear; high 30: every enemy who can hear) combined with a key (eight, each tied to a damage type, status, Attribute and recovery) and a tone (seven general effects). First level learns all three volumes plus one key and one tone; each further level adds a key or a tone.

After your verse affects one or more enemies, with an arcane weapon equipped, choose one until the start of your next turn: allies deal (SL) extra damage to those enemies; or you recover (SL) MP each time one of them suffers damage (per enemy, when one source hits several).
After you sing a verse at medium or high volume, all physical damage you suffer until the start of your next turn is reduced by (SL), applied before Affinities.
After you sing a verse at low or medium volume, perform a free attack with an equipped weapon once the verse resolves, treating your High Roll as 0 for damage.

Once per scene, as your action, spend 1 Fabula Point to repeat the most recent action taken by another character this scene, paying all costs. Never: Quirks or anything derived from one, Champion/Villain uniques, Equipment actions, rituals/Projects/anything outside a conflict, or a Guise swap.
+(SL) to the leader's Group Check. Counts toward the two-effect cap.

Declare an action and a trigger condition; when the trigger occurs, perform it immediately, resolving before the triggering action completes. +(SL) to related Checks. The declaration is lost when your next turn starts.

Unobserved by anyone outside your party, spend 1 Fabula Point to assume the appearance of a humanoid seen within the past two days; +(SL) to impersonation Checks. Lasts until dropped or seen through; the Mask never covers a Guise's Tell; stacks with the Many Faces Perk (the Perk gives the face, this gives the performance).
Spend 2 IP and choose the target, then roll 1d4: 1 — recover (SL × 10) HP and MP; 2 — recover from all status effects and gain 1 IP; 3 — (SL × 10) poison damage; 4 — inflict poisoned and enraged.

The engine. Gain (SL) ingredients when resting in a settlement; carry up to 10 + (SL × 5), and they never spoil. Action: combine 2–3 ingredients into a delicacy, then apply it to yourself or an ally you can see — or make a damageless free attack that applies it to each enemy hit.
Cooking's free attack may deal real damage (High Roll treated as 0) if the delicacy used at most 2 ingredients.
When applying a delicacy to yourself or an ally, spend up to (SL × 10) MP: every 10 MP feeds one additional ally you can see.
When preparing a delicacy, spend 2 IP to change one ingredient's taste to any taste you choose.
After each travel roll, gain (SL × 2) ingredients (requires Cooking).

Once per non-conflict scene in a populated place, pick up a package (carry up to five; lost only through Surrender), establishing where and/or to whom it goes. On delivery choose: 1 Fabula Point, (level × 10) zenit, or gain/strengthen a Bond with an NPC, location or organization relevant to the delivery.

On a rest, forgo normal restoration — regain only (SL × 10) HP and MP and recover from (SL) statuses (Bond adjustment keeps) — to choose an area within one travel day (further if your travel means reach further): reroll its next travel die; ask one honestly-answered question; or pick up/deliver a package there.

✎(capped at SL2; printed SL3) While carrying two or fewer packages, move one extra travel day's distance on the world map. While carrying three or more, treat your maximum HP and MP as (SL × 5) higher.

Travel and rest services cost (SL × 10) zenit less for you and your group, to a minimum of half price. After a rest or travel roll using such a paid service, +(SL) on your next Check. Counts toward the two-effect cap.

When you pick up a package, spend 1 Fabula Point to declare it rare equipment you can equip, chosen by the GM, worth up to ((level + SL) × 50) zenit. Only you may equip it; one package at a time; the loan ends on delivery. Never a hoplosphere or sphere-bearing gear.

Action + 10 MP: offer a blessing to your allies — never yourself — each freely refusing or accepting. Each accepter gains +(SL × 3) HP/MP recovery and −(SL) damage taken until scene's end, and owes a gift you name, due before their next rest — or the blessing turns curse: −(SL × 3) recovery and +(SL) damage taken until that rest.

Ask an ally or NPC a favour — no cost, no action. If they accept and fulfil it, you owe them on their terms, under a GM-set penalty until repaid. The favour may always be refused, and an unfulfillable ask costs nothing.

See the hidden gates of the fairy paths — shortcuts with a price. Deliberately numberless: form, destination and consequences are the GM's, ruled once per campaign (here: Risky Passage — each use carries a minor cost or complication).

Each level attunes one element (of eight) among spells you know; its fey effect rides those spells free: air lifts an ally into flight for a turn, bolt lets an ally act right after you, fire adds a burn next turn, ice shields an ally for −5 damage, poison poisons — and dark, earth and light each deny one action type (Ranged, Melee, Spell) for the target's next turn.
Whenever you recover Mind Points, recover an additional (SL × 4) — any source, no limit.

Each level teaches one dance (of seventeen). On your turn, with no martial armor equipped, spend 10 MP to perform one you know — no action required, once per turn; 5 MP if you performed a different dance on your previous turn this scene.
After a dance, your attacks with brawling, dagger, flail, sword and thrown weapons deal (SL) extra damage until your next turn; with an arcane weapon equipped, offensive spells too.
After a dance with until-your-next-turn duration, +(SL × 2) to Opposed Checks relying on acrobatics, coordination or speed, until your next turn.
When performing a lasting dance, spend 10 MP: one ally you can see toward whom you hold a Bond of affection gains its benefits too, same duration.
After a dance, perform the Equipment action for free. Swapping Guise this way still triggers the Turn — once per conflict, exactly as ruled.

Action + 5 MP: draw on one of the scene's wellsprings and apply an invocation to a creature you can see. SL1 reaches "blast" invocations, SL2 adds "hex", SL3 all. Scaling: damage +5/+10 at level 20+/40+; HP recovery and MP loss +10/+20.
When you invoke, spend up to (SL × 10) extra MP; every 10 MP adds one more target you can see.
Always communicate with elementals. When your invocation or spell restores HP with an elemental present on the scene, it restores (SL × 5) more.

After an ally's damage — increased by one or more of your "hex" invocations — costs an enemy HP: free attack against that enemy only, at +(SL) Accuracy. On a hit its damage becomes the ally's type, and all your hexes on the target end once it resolves.
With an arcane, bow, brawling, flail, sword or thrown weapon equipped: "blast" invocations deal (SL) extra damage, and your "hex" invocations grant (5 + SL) extra damage instead of 5.
Each level learns one Elementalist spell. Offensive spells use (INS + WLP) for the Magic Check.
Casting an Instantaneous spell with an arcane weapon equipped: raise its cost by up to (SL × 10) MP for +5 damage per extra 10 MP.
Offensive spells cast with an arcane weapon equipped gain +(SL × 2) to the Magic Check.
Single-target offensive spells costing (SL × 20) MP or less may roll the Magic Check on an equipped non-arcane weapon's Accuracy formula, +(SL) if that formula uses Dexterity.
When performing a Ritual, +10 MP stores it in a scroll (hold up to SL). Whoever holds the scroll releases it for 10 MP; used in conflict it takes an action and a Clock as normal. Destroyed on use.
On a rest, take a spark of Air, Earth, Fire or Water. Spend it once before your next rest for that element's effect — die replacement, damage reduction, and kin.
Once per conflict scene, while in Crisis: perform an additional action on your turn, which must be the Inventory action.
Choose a gadget type — alchemy, infusions or magitech — and gain its basic benefits. Each further level buys a new type's basics, or upgrades one you have to advanced, then superior.
Your potions that restore one creature's HP/MP may affect up to (SL) additional creatures, at half effect for everyone.
Your restorative magispheres and potions restore (SL × 5) more HP/MP; your elemental shards, magispheres and potions deal (SL) extra damage.
Projects you work on auto-pay up to (SL × 100) zenit of material costs and gain (SL) extra progress per day. Makes a Project-holder better — never grants Project access.
Destroy an item worth 100z+ that you own (never an IP-crafted one) to regain (value ÷ 100) IP, +1 IP if it cost at most (SL × 200)z. In conflict this rides an Inventory action.

When progressing a Project, opt for +2 progress and roll d8: at or under (SL), the invention gains a one-use bonus function; 7–8, the Project stalls until a condition is met. Does nothing without the Projects pool pick.
Each level learns one Entropist spell. Offensive spells use (INS + WLP) for the Magic Check.
After you suffer damage, recover (SL × 2) MP.

You have a lucky number — 7 at each session's start. Once per scene, after rolling a Check, replace one die's value with it (impossible values allowed); the replaced value becomes your new lucky number.

Action + up to (SL × 5) MP; each 5 MP buys one option, once each: inflict slow; cure slow; a slowed enemy loses (10 + SL × 5) HP; a creature takes a free Equipment action; an ally yet to act takes their turn after yours. Variant available: Second Slicer — free attack, +(SL) Accuracy, inflicts slow with riders. Chosen permanently.

When performing a Ritual, after paying MP: grow its area one stage free, rolling a d20 beside the Magic Check — beat the Check's result or hit its difficulty exactly and the Ritual misfires catastrophically.
Settlements you rest in become points of light: speak with familiar people across any of them at any distance, and the group's costs to rest, resupply IP or secure lodging fall while inside one.

Action + 5 MP to enter. While in it, Defense and Magic Defense both become (9 + SL) — (10 + SL) at level 20+, (11 + SL) at 40+; the flat value replaces the score and nothing may be added to it. On leaving, choose one: a free attack with an equipped weapon, or a single-target spell costing (SL × 5) MP or less — High Roll treated as 0 either way.
After you take damage, spend 5 MP to enter. While in it you deal (SL) extra damage from all sources — and take (SL) extra damage from all sources.

Begin each conflict with (SL) Tempo; +1 when an enemy misses you in Parry Stance, +1 when you deal damage in Lunge Stance. Enter at the start of your turn by spending 7 Tempo: Attribute dice one size higher (max d12) and all damage doubled before Affinities, until end of turn.
While in a Stance, you may Guard and spend 10 MP to exit it.

Spend 10 MP at the start of a conflict to enter Parry or Lunge Stance immediately. Exiting one Stance by entering another recovers you from one status effect. Triggers on the Turn when swapping in mid-conflict.
Each level discovers one magiseed type. In a conflict, if your garden is empty: action + 20 MP plants a magiseed you have discovered.

After planting through Chloromancy (not Graft), choose one: a free attack with an equipped weapon, or the Spell action for free casting a spell of (5 + SL × 5) MP or less (you still pay it). High Roll treated as 0 either way.
With a magiseed in your garden and 1+ Growth Clock sections filled, action: swap it for a different magiseed you have discovered, keeping the filled sections unchanged.
When a magiseed is removed from your garden, one creature you can see that is in Crisis recovers (5 + SL × 5) HP.

Grants Rituals of the Ritualism discipline, extended to creating, animating and controlling vegetation, pollen, spores and toxins — never plant-Species NPCs. Runs under the standing rulings that keep it inside the benefit-pool architecture.
While in Crisis, +(SL × 2) damage — attacks, spells, Arcana, items, anything.

Accuracy Checks with brawling, dagger, flail and thrown weapons crit on doubles (when not a fumble). Two adopted alternates exist — Brave Brawler and Meteor Slam (SL3 caps); take at most one, chosen permanently.
When you spend a Fabula Point to invoke a Bond or Trait: recover (SL × 5) HP, or (SL × 5) MP, or shake one status effect.
Action + 5 MP: Opposed (MIG + WLP) Check (+SL) against an enemy you can see. Success: they are enraged, fixed on you, and must include you in their attacks and offensive spells while it lasts.
Guarding without covering anyone: recover (5 + SL × your highest Bond strength) HP, and raise Might or Willpower one die size (max d12) until your next turn.

When you cause mayhem to draw attention, up to (SL) other characters each generate an opportunity — plus one once-per-session pick: 1 Fabula Point, a worthy NPC appears, or someone looking to hire you.
Get in someone's face to Study them with (MIG + MIG), and ask the GM up to (SL) questions about their motivations, connections or fighting style — answered truthfully.

When you Guard and cover an ally, they gain Resistance to all damage types until your next turn. Alternate: Agile Defender — armourless, shieldless; Protect refreshes on a miss and +(SL + 1) to both Defenses while protecting. Chosen permanently.
With a shield or martial armour equipped, all damage you suffer is reduced by (SL), before Affinities.
A shield may fill your main hand. With two shields: both items' benefits, treated together as Twin Shields — (MIG + MIG), (HR + 5) physical, +Defensive Mastery SL damage.
Permanently +(SL × 3) max HP.
Take another creature's place against an attack, spell or danger — declared before or after its Checks. If it already hit you, it hits you twice. In conflict, once until the start of your next turn.
Rest in a populated area without recovering HP/MP to keep watch: identify the area's greatest threat and a clue to its current work, and ward a landmark.
Once per session, when you risk yourself for a non-PC you hold a Bond of hatred or mistrust toward: gain 1 Fabula Point, then immediately add or change one emotion in that Bond.
One Illusionist spell per Skill Level (twelve exist against a ten-level cap — nobody ever learns the list). Offensive Illusionist spells and Phantasms use (INS + WLP).
Once per round, after your Phantasms shatter as part of a Command spell, gain one Residue (hold up to SL). When casting, spend any number: −2 MP each.
Shatter one of your Phantasms to recover (SL × 5) HP.
When you cast a spell and cannot afford its total MP cost, shatter one of your Phantasms for a 10 MP bonus toward it — never to create a Phantasm. Triggers only on a genuine shortfall, not by choice.
At the start of a conflict scene, spend 10 MP to create one Phantasm. Triggers on the Turn when swapping in mid-conflict.

You may perform Rituals of the Ritualism discipline (the Keeper is a ritual-granting class; this class skill is the route, so no benefit pick is committed and no discipline is closed to the party). Bind your soul to Sanctuaries — small places of spiritual and historical weight, found through story; each carries a Haunt and a Ritual. In a conflict: action + 5/10/15 MP (escalating within a turn, resetting each turn) Haunts a creature you hold a Bond with — never yourself — at any distance. One creature per Sanctuary, one Sanctuary per creature; banishing is free on your turn.
While you are in Crisis, Haunting costs (SL) MP less — or (SL × 2) less if the creature you are Haunting is also in Crisis. Minimum 0.

On a rest, set a condition describing a creature. When such a creature tries to enter your Sanctuary: you know, wherever you are, and it must beat you in an Opposed (WLP + WLP) Check — you at +(SL × 2) — or be repelled until sunrise. Once per creature per night; a Villain may spend 1 Ultima Point to force through.

A willing NPC in your Sanctuary may extract and grant you their Soul Treasure — no forcing, no persuading. While it is equipped or in your pack, you may Haunt them as though your Bond were strength 1, or your real Bond if higher. A Soul Treasure is that creature's hoplosphere.

Rituals performed in your Sanctuary read each helper's Bond toward you: −(SL) MP per positive emotion (capped at 3 per helper), +(SL × 2) MP per negative emotion, uncapped. Choose your assistants carefully, or perform alone.

Each level learns one law (of eight). At the start of a conflict scene, enact up to two laws you know; an action + 10 MP enacts another. A broken law is removed until enacted again; enacting an already-active law does nothing; any Magistrate may respond to any active law, whoever enacted it.
(Requires Letter of the Law) When you hit a creature with an attack or offensive spell, spend up to (SL × 20) MP: immediately enact one law you know for every 20 MP spent.

(Requires Letter of the Law) A law-breaker receives a citation once the break resolves: the next damage they take is increased by (SL × 2) — (SL × 5) if that damage came from breaking another law — then the citation is removed. Cited damage ignores Resistances, as printed. All citations clear at scene's end.
(Requires Letter of the Law) When an enemy breaks a law, you may choose an ally who can see you instead of making the attack-or-spell response against the breaker: that ally regains (SL × 5) HP.

At no MP cost, Guard: until your next turn, broken laws are not removed from the scene; then at the start of that turn, make a free attack with an equipped weapon against one enemy that broke one or more laws.

Action + 10 MP: choose dazed, shaken, slow or weak. At the start of each of your later turns this conflict, every enemy suffering it takes (SL × 3) damage — no Check, no roll; the type matches an equipped weapon, else physical. One status at a time; an action switches it.
When a Villain enters a scene you are in, spend a Fabula Point to learn that Villain's goal for the scene.

✎(printed SL10 for twelve spells; lowered to 9 — one level per spell, and the folded list holds nine; returns to 10 if a tenth spell earns its way in) Each level teaches one Malefaction spell. Offensive Malefaction spells use (INS + WLP).

Casting an offensive single-target spell, before rolling: declare the Check an automatic success — at the cost of suffering the spell's effects yourself, High Roll 0 for both. If the spell could not affect you at all, it fails and neither of you is affected.

Unarmed strikes deal +(6 + SL × 2) damage and gain +(SL) Accuracy, but refuse extra damage from Quirks. Start of each conflict turn: declare them a different weapon Category until your next turn — bow, firearm or thrown makes them ranged.
While in Crisis, when your attack or offensive spell costs one or more enemies HP, recover (SL × 5) HP.
After losing HP to typed non-physical damage, shed 10 HP to gain Resistance to that type until the next time you use this Skill.
Damaging NPCs reveals their Species, and the GM names (SL) fitting therioforms. With Theriomorphosis, pay its cost on the spot to wear them — learned or not.

Each level teaches one therioform. Action + flat 20 HP: manifest up to two therioforms immediately, then a free attack with High Roll treated as 0. Forms last the scene; they end on death, unconsciousness, Guard, or re-use; 10 MP at scene's end carries them forward.

Choose a Species Forte — never humanoid. Once per scene, create a Bond of admiration or inferiority toward a Forte creature whose presence or signs you are aware of: your Quarry, at +(SL) to track, locate, identify and Study. Absent Quarry: action + 1 Fabula Point learns its direction plus a free remote Study. If no Bond can form, the Species is not present and did not pass through.
While no equipment fixes your Magic Defense to a flat value, +(SL) Magic Defense — +(SL + 1) against creatures of your Forte.

The four Hunter Rituals only, in a discipline flavour of your choice: Arm Up (a community gains +5 damage vs your Forte via a swapped weapon Quality), Freedom (release a controlled or possessed creature; fails if it takes damage during the performance), Smoke Out (Forte creatures in the area must reveal themselves; a Villain may spend an Ultima Point to stay hidden), Land Survey (know the ritual area like the back of your hand). Helpers' IP cuts the MP cost, 10 per point.

On first take choose a track — Slaying, Research or Taming — gaining its basic tier; each level buys a new track's basics or upgrades one to advanced, then superior. Slaying: 2-IP hit-laced infusions, +5 damage (+10 vs Forte) with riders — superior tier ruled legal 6 Aug: Engineered inflicts through status immunity as printed (no Pressure interaction), Adaptive allowed. Research: cheaper Forte consumables, the spectrographic camera, the travelling lab. Taming: spoken commands to soldier-rank Forte creatures, then Capture (Companions on Loyalty Points, max three), then the Menagerie.

Identify your Forte's Species on sight, and see when a visible creature is possessed or controlled. The first time each scene you Study a Forte creature (not via Avid Seeker or a spectrograph), ask up to (SL) questions about its condition, motives or emotions.

Action + 5 MP: Opposed (INS + WLP) Check (+SL) against an enemy that hears and understands you. Success: they lose (SL × 5) MP, suffer dazed or shaken (your choice), and all sources deal +(SL) damage to them until your next turn.
Action + 5 MP: an ally who hears you recovers (SL × 10) HP and, in conflict, raises a chosen Attribute one die size (max d12) until your next turn.

When another PC who can hear you rolls a Check, spend 1 Fabula Point invoking one of their Traits or Bonds to let them reroll or improve the Result. With a Bond toward them, they also recover (SL × 10) MP.
On a successful Clock Check that relied on charm, diplomacy, deception or intimidation: spend up to (SL × 20) MP, moving 1 extra section per 20 MP.
Action + 15 MP: create an Inspiration Clock of (SL) sections lasting until you rest or it fills. When an ally would suffer a status, fill a section instead — the status lands on you as normal.
Record each Theme change and its cause. Every 5 recorded changes: each player gains (SL) XP and you gain an additional Identity built from the story your Themes tell.

When a creature's spell includes you among its targets, the caster may spend up to (SL) HP: you recover 2 HP per HP spent, or shed one status per 3 HP. When an offensive spell includes you, you may spend up to (SL) HP to deal 2 dark damage per HP back at the caster — 3 per HP at level 40+.
Communicate with beast, demon and undead creatures. A mindless undead can be read for whether it is commanded, and what its orders are.

Choose a Craving: Mesmerizing (dazed, MP-primary), Pestilent (weak, HP-primary; printed Miasmic), Terrifying (shaken, MP-primary) or Inevitable (slow, HP-primary). First infliction of its status on an unmarked creature each scene marks it and pays (SL × 5) primary or (SL × 3) secondary; at SL3+ the Craving's second status also triggers. Marks vanish at scene's end. Undead and constructs are not meals (house ruling — not in print).

Your Craving's active half (its own SL): Mesmerizing — 5 MP on an Opposed Check inflicts dazed, subtly (+SL to stay unnoticed); Pestilent — 5 MP at round start, every weak creature, friend or foe, takes (SL × 2) poison (× 4 at level 40+) and you recover half as HP; Terrifying — +(SL) damage per shaken creature in the scene, friend or foe; Inevitable — in a chase, spend up to (SL × 20) MP: per 20, inflict slow or fill a pursuit-clock section.

After your first surrender in a scene, at the start of a later round spend 1 Fabula Point to rise with (Crisis value + SL × 2) HP. Surrender's consequence still lands, and the wrong-way point ticks the Miasma Clock. Fall to 0 again and you leave the scene — cleanly, no further payout.
Choose an element at acquisition (air, bolt, dark, earth, fire, ice or light). Grants the Panoply and the Token; each level adds an enchantment.

When a damaging spell you cast in the Panoply hits and its Magic Check invoked a Bond of admiration, loyalty and/or affection: +(SL) damage, and the spell ignores Immunities and Resistances, as printed.
Your Panoply entry damage may instead heal — chosen targets gain Absorption against that instance.
In the Panoply, casting a non-offensive spell of 10+ MP recovers (SL × 2) MP.
When a creature makes a Magic Check, spend a Fabula Point and choose a Bonded ally you can see: +(2 + Bond strength) Magic Defense against it — a hit may become a miss. Once per round.

Perform Medical Procedures: ritual mechanics on a Medical Check — (DEX + INS) or (INS + INS) — costed in zenit or IP at the GM's call. Minor (100z / 3 IP, DL 7) through Extreme (800z / 6 IP, DL 16): a set dislocation up to transplants and cures. The zenit is the practitioner's cost; a client's bill is the fee schedule (economy pass §1).

Each level stocks two catalogue entries — potions, elixirs and the period-renamed preparations (Sal Volatile, Liniment, Coca Elixir, Quinine Wine, Carbolic Preparation, Steadying Drops, Antitoxin…), created and used via the Inventory action. Vinum Ferri prints a duplicated effect — named, unusable until errata.
When you create a potion, combine it with up to (SL) Pharmaceuticals; the result carries all component effects and all component IP costs, plus any listed synergy.
When your item or spell restores HP and/or MP to a target in Crisis, they recover +(SL × 5).

Carry +(SL × 2) IP, ring-fenced for Pharmaceuticals and Drug Synthesis items; taken at creation, they arrive stocked. The satchel and its current stock ride the Guise. Capacity, not supply — refills cost 10z a point.
On a melee attack, spend 10 MP: the attack gains multi (2), or its multi rises by one (max 3).
On a damaging melee hit, trade all its damage for one option: dazed on each target; weak on each target; or each target loses (SL × 10) MP.

Action + 10 MP: free single-target melee attack. On a hit choose: +(SL × 5) damage ignoring Resistances but also non-physical Vulnerabilities; or no damage, and your allies deal +(SL × 2) to the target until your next turn.
After an enemy's melee attack hits or misses you with an even Accuracy Result: free melee attack back at them alone, High Roll treated as 0.
+(SL) to all Accuracy Checks with melee weapons.

On finishing a rest, swear to protect someone you hold admiration, loyalty or affection toward: that Bond counts 1 stronger until your next rest, and they may transfer up to (SL × 5) of any HP/MP loss to you.
Incorporate an organisation — one at a time. Once per session, use one organisational ability as a free action on your turn by spending 1 IP.
Spend 1 IP to activate an organisational ability as a free action, (SL) times per session — in addition to Incorporate's single free use.

Personal purchases cost (SL × 10%) less; personal payments and rewards pay (SL × 10%) more. At GM discretion it also bends narrative expense and reward, or grants +(SL) to related Checks — read as transactions only.

Once per conflict scene, as part of an action, spend up to (SL × 200) zenit before rolling: +1 per 200 spent, narratively explained. Kept — it makes the price of privilege legible, out loud. Counts toward the two-effect cap.
Once per conflict scene, take the Inventory action to restore up to 2 IP, divided between up to two creatures including yourself.

The Grave Point skill. After a creature you can see loses HP, if it is in Crisis and not undead: gain 1 Grave Point, holding up to (SL + 1). When you hit 0 HP you lose all points — the first time each scene, if you lost at least one, your HP becomes (SL × points lost) instead. That substitution lands at 0 HP, so you never reach the Surrender-or-Sacrifice choice: Reaping prevents the fall rather than reversing it, and the Miasma Clock does not tick. Later falls in the same scene are ordinary, and those Surrenders land in full.
Always communicate with undead creatures. Once per scene, ask an undead a single question; it is compelled to answer truthfully.
After you cause one or more enemies to lose HP, if at least one is shaken and/or weak: gain 1 Grave Point and recover (SL × 2) MP.

When your spell damages one or more enemies, spend 1 Grave Point and choose one: pick a damaged enemy — the spell deals extra damage to each damaged enemy equal to (SL + that enemy's status count); or every damaged enemy suffers shaken after the spell resolves.

When you cast an offensive "one creature" spell, spend 2 Grave Points: it targets every creature present in the scene — allies included — one Magic Check compared against each Magic Defense. All its damage becomes dark and cannot change type.
A single-target hit on a creature suffering statuses may deal +(SL + number of its statuses) damage.
With no shield and no martial armour equipped, +(SL) Defense.
Start of conflict, 10 MP: before round one, a free attack or a free Hinder/Objective action, with +(SL) to its Checks.

Action: (DEX + WLP) Check (+SL) vs an enemy's Magic Defense. Success: a soldier yields (SL) IP; an elite or champion yields a soul treasure worth up to (level × 30, ×50 for Villains). Once per creature. Takes the hoplosphere drop — one body, one clot.

When two or more NPCs instigate trouble, up to (SL) soldier-rank creatures hesitate — you gain an opportunity, and in a conflict they cannot attack or cast offensively on their first turn. Creatures 5+ levels above you are immune.
When you or an ally Checks to move a Clock and quick thinking could help: spend up to (SL × 10) MP, +1 to the Result per 10 MP — enough to turn failure into success or buy extra sections.

Start of your conflict turn: your focus is one ally able to hear you, or one enemy you can see suffering dazed, enraged and/or shaken. Until your next turn, +(SL) to Checks to examine the focus and to Accuracy/Magic Checks for attacks and offensive spells that include it.
Spells and verses that include your focus among their targets cost (SL) less MP — (SL × 2) less if the focus is the only target — to a minimum of 0.

Telepathy with any conscious ally within the same district; you count as hearing each other for Skills and effects. Ritualism for Aether purposes only — transport, information and tracking within the Aether.
Each level grants one of the nine gifts: event-triggered reactions with an MP cost, scaling with the Brainwave Clock (4 sections, empty at the start of each scene).
Accuracy Checks may replace one Attribute die with Willpower.
On a ranged attack, spend 10 MP: the attack gains multi (2), or its multi rises by one (max 3).
After any visible creature's ranged Accuracy Check: spend (5 + the Result) MP to make the attack miss everyone. Needs a ranged weapon equipped; useless against crits.
Guarding without covering anyone: bank +(SL × 3) damage on your next ranged attack this scene, or take a free bow/firearm attack with High Roll treated as 0.
+(SL) to all Accuracy Checks with ranged weapons.
On a damaging ranged hit, trade all its damage for one option: shaken on each target; slow on each target; or each target loses (SL × 10) MP.
When a travel roll turns up danger: every other group member gains +(SL) on their next non-offensive Check, or takes (SL × 2) less from the next damage that reaches them.
Rest in a populated area to ask the GM for an open bounty: a target and a condition. Fulfil it before your next rest for (SL × 100) zenit.

Each level learns one Sin-Eater spell. Offensive Sin-Eater spells use (MIG + WLP); Sin-Eater spells cost Hit Points instead of MP, and anything that references, changes or ignores MP costs applies to their HP costs instead.

Action: roll your current Might die and lose that many HP. If not reduced to 0, immediately perform the Spell action for free (costs still paid); every target that spell affected then suffers (SL + the roll) poison damage.

At conflict start, spend 10 HP: cast a spell of (10 × SL) total cost or less as a runic spell, paid upfront, and name a trigger. The first time it is met the spell must release, free — targets chosen then. Still held at scene's end: lost, and you recover 5 HP.

Whenever you deal damage, deal extra damage equal to the number of Ultima Points spent this session. The Miasma clause is struck (13 Aug 2026): a Villain spending an Ultima Point does not tick the Miasma Clock unless a specific boss skill says so.
When your offensive spell damages creatures and none was Vulnerable to any damage suffered, choose up to (SL) damage types: the GM reveals those creatures' Affinities toward them.

Each level chooses a creature Species. Action + 2 IP oils a weapon equipped by you or a willing creature (a free attack rides along if the weapon is yours). Until scene's end, when the oil's Species is hit by that weapon the attacker picks one: slow; weak; strip one damage Resistance for the scene; or fill 1 Pressure Clock section (house-added fourth option).

On an Accuracy, Magic or contested Check, spend 1 Fabula Point and invoke one of the target's Traits: +(SL) to your Result against that target. A Villain may spend an Ultima Point to cancel. The Miasma clause is struck (13 Aug 2026): that spend no longer ticks the Miasma Clock.
(Single level) When you hit a non-soldier creature with a damaging attack, deal extra damage equal to (2 × the number of soldiers it replaces).
When you hit a creature, spend 10 MP and choose one of its basic attacks or spells: until the start of your next turn it deals (SL × 2) less damage with that action.
When you rest in the wilderness, ask the GM up to (SL) questions about creatures in the area, answered truthfully.
Each level learns one Spiritist spell. Offensive spells use (INS + WLP) for the Magic Check.
Spells targeting allies, with an arcane weapon equipped: each of those allies also recovers (3 + SL × your number of Bonds) HP.
Spells targeting allies, with an arcane weapon equipped: one targeted ally you have a Bond towards gains a bonus on their next Check this scene equal to that Bond's strength.
Short on MP, pay (10 + the spell's total MP cost) in HP instead — but the spell then recovers no HP for you.

Invoking a Bond triggers one of its emotions' effects — not optional. Admiration seeds opportunities; inferiority hands out fumble triggers; Loyalty no longer costs the supporter their turn; each emotion has its own clause.
Rituals cost (SL × 4) less MP, and shortfalls may be paid in HP — even to 0, at the price of Sacrificing yourself.
+(SL) Bond slots. When you invoke a Bond to improve an attack's Accuracy, that attack deals additional damage equal to the Bond's strength.
When you invoke a Bond, an ally recovers (SL × 4) HP or MP — and both if the Bond is with them.
Once per session, spend a Fabula Point to create a Bond, or to add an emotion to an existing one.

Once per session, gain (SL) Fabula Points for saving NPCs from danger, completing a quest for them, or being present when a Villain runs out of Ultima Points. These Fabula Points do not tick the Miasma Clock.
Action + a Fabula Point: recover from all status effects and regain (10 + SL × 10) MP.

Each level teaches two symbols; (SL + 1) may be active at once. Inventory action + 2 IP creates one you know, then: apply it to yourself; apply it to an ally you can see; or perform a damageless free attack that copies it onto every enemy hit — each copy counting against the limit.
When a creature you can see bearing one of your symbols suffers damage or recovers HP/MP, you may have it suffer (SL) extra damage or recover (SL) more, respectively.

An ally bearing your symbol may take the Spell action and destroy that symbol to cast a spell you know of (SL × 10) MP or less — the ally pays the MP. Allowed on the Ritual Scrolls precedent. Requires you to know spells from another class.
You always know the exact direction to any creature bearing one of your symbols within 2 travel days. One symbol per creature — a newer mark from any source erases yours.
Regain (SL) Inventory Points after each travel roll.
Resting at an inn or tavern: ask the GM up to (SL) questions about the area and its people, answered truthfully.
On the world map, your group makes a discovery on a travel roll of (SL + 1) or lower, instead of only on a 1.
Your travel rolls use a die one size smaller (min d6). Multiple holders don't stack.

Once per session, at a hidden place of breathtaking beauty or revelation 5+ travel days from anywhere: choose up to (SL) distinct one-time benefits — full HP for one character, full MP for another, and kin.

The Well caps at your Crisis score, empties at every rest, and pays any Skill that spends HP. Fill it by being overhealed (spend MP equal to half the excess) — or by feeding: an interlude, never a conflict action; a willing donor spends the HP and marks their Bond toward you, a stranger fills it free and ticks that district's Miasma Clock. Spend it: once per turn, soak damage on you or another before it lands; add half-spent-HP extra damage on a successful attack or offensive spell; or an action heals you or an ally for half the HP spent.

Each level teaches one malediction (of eight — full text in the spell list). Maledictions follow spell rules but cost Hit Points, use (MIG + WLP) offensively, and are lifted by filling a negotiated 4-section Clock. Harm is retyped to dark; Reanimate raises one corpse at a time.

Action: Opposed (MIG + WLP) Check against a creature you can touch. On success choose exactly one: drain HR Hit Points and recover half; or inflict dazed/shaken/slow/weak and treat the matching Attribute die (INS/WLP/DEX/MIG) one size higher until they recover — capped at d12. Heals you directly; never touches the Well. Counts toward the two-effect cap.
In a conflict, action: spend up to (SL × 10) Hit Points and take one return — recover half the HP spent as MP, or recharge 1 IP per 20 HP spent.

After a beast, monster or plant you can see resolves a spell, learn it (recording the Species). Hold up to (SL + 2); offensive casts use your chosen (INS + WLP) or (MIG + WLP). Variant available: Spell Buffet — read non-humanoid HP at (15 + half level) or less, execute one to learn all its spells, keeping (SL + 4). Chosen permanently.
After your spell damages one or more creatures, with an arcane, dagger or flail weapon equipped: recover (SL × 2) MP.
You can always communicate with beasts, monsters and plants.
Your Chimerist spells poison each damaged creature that shares its Species with the creature you learned the spell from.

✎(Noncombat supplement, amended — the +(SL) max IP is Guise-bound, rising while that Guise is worn) Spend 2 IP on food that draws nearby animals to perform a simple task, comparable to a Minor Ritual.
Record Traits you learn from visible beasts, monsters and plants. Invoke one for 15 MP or 1 Fabula Point to mimic the creature — one impressive feat within that Trait's bounds, statistics unchanged.

Choose a Hound: Above (the licensed world), Below (a named monster that knows your address), Beyond (the Aether's attention) or Within (the uncounted). Once per scene, when events match it, gain (SL) Rabbit Points — spend after seeing a roll, before any Fabula reroll, at +1 each on your Hound's Check types. Once per session, 1 Fabula Point summons the Hound if plausible (a GM veto refunds the point); a public, monstrous arrival runs the ordinary Miasma and Tell machinery.

When you are blocked from escaping a conflict scene — by barrier, by danger, or by an obligation of your own Identity or Theme — you deal +(SL) damage and gain +(SL) to Checks made as part of the Hinder action.

On another creature's turn, spend 1 Fabula Point: they use their action to escape the scene, reappearing where a Player Character is present. No other character may use this on you that scene; locked out beside the Rogue's See You Later. It saves anyone but its user.

Once per scene, when a friendly PC completes a Clock with a successful Check or an elite-or-higher enemy first enters Crisis, choose one: every friendly PC recovers (SL × 4) HP or MP, each choosing which (SL × 6 at level 40+); every friendly PC recovers from up to (SL) statuses; or the triggering character gains +(SL) to their next Check.

At conflict start, spend 10 MP to perform Guard, Objective or Study before round one, at +(SL) to its Checks. Locked out beside the Rogue's High Speed and the Naturalist's post-Initiative camera shot — one pre-round trick per character. Triggers on the Turn when swapping in mid-conflict.

Each time the party returns to a community you have history with, generate two things: one NPC from your past (ally, debtor, or rival — your choice of type), and one complication arising from your presence (a debt called in, a bounty, a contact the wrong people know about). The GM and player agree the specifics; the complication is mandatory.
Gain +(SL × 2) on checks to pick locks, disable traps, find security weaknesses, or damage infrastructure without being detected.
When you damage a creature that actively serves an authority figure (a constable, a Foundry enforcer, a noble's bodyguard), deal +(SL × 3) bonus typeless damage and ignore Resistances on that attack.
Spend (SL × 5) MP. Ask the GM up to (SL) questions about an NPC's behaviour, motivations, or likely next move. The GM must answer honestly.

When purchasing goods or services in a settlement where rebel, radical, or underground factions operate, reduce the cost by (SL × 20)%. Faction contacts may offer startup resources (tools, safe houses, introductions) at GM discretion.

Travel checks in settlements where you are known as a troublemaker are made with advantage (roll twice, keep the better result). You are never surprised in a location where your reputation precedes you. At SL4, your infamy reaches across the city — no settlement in the campaign is unknown to you.

At the start of a conflict in a settlement you have tagged (graffiti, a calling card, a known haunt), every soldier-rank enemy must make a Resolve check or be Shaken for the first round. You may tag a settlement between scenes without rolling.

When you take the Assist action on an ally's spell, that spell gains: +2 to the caster's Magic Check (SL1); the spell deals or heals +(SL × 5) (SL2); the spell's MP cost is reduced by (SL × 5) (SL3). All unlocked benefits apply at the appropriate SL.
When working on a ritual clock, spend (SL × 5) MP to mark an additional segment beyond the action's normal yield.
Reaction: spend (SL × 10) MP. Remove up to (SL) willing creatures from the target list of a hostile spell before it resolves. Cannot remove the caster themselves.
You gain +(SL) on all ritual checks. The zenit cost of any ritual you participate in is reduced by (SL × 50), minimum 0.
When you assist an ally's check (any type), your bonus is increased by +1 per 3 points by which your result exceeds the difficulty (max bonus +(SL)).
Whenever you spend a Fabula Point in a conflict, gain 2 IP as well.
As an action, produce two Inventory-tier items simultaneously. Their effects both apply (or both activate on a target of your choice).
When you try to fill or erase a clock through deception or comic misdirection, roll 1d3. Optionally apply that result as a bonus or penalty to your check — your choice after seeing the die.

Declare any check a deliberate fumble before rolling. The fumble triggers normally (Opportunity for the GM, FP earned for you). You additionally choose which Opportunity the GM takes (from a list you agree on). An ally of your choice immediately recovers 10 MP.
Spend (SL × 5) MP. A creature that can hear you takes −(SL) to its next check this round.

Free weapon attack with a dagger, brawling weapon, or thrown weapon. Spend MP (up to SL × 5) for a bonus on the Accuracy Check equal to MP spent ÷ 5. If your result beats the target's Defense by 5 or more, the damage ignores all Affinities and is multiplied × (1 + SL ÷ 5, rounded down, max ×3).
As an action, make an open check with your INS die vs a difficulty of 10. On success, you cannot be targeted by enemies until you make an offensive action or the scene ends.
On your first turn of a conflict, or when any of your actions targets a creature that cannot see you, gain +(SL) on Accuracy Checks and Magic Checks.

Spend 1 FP to establish a fully worked-out alternate persona. Write it down: name, profession, plausible history, one known contact. The identity holds until a Villain spends an Ultima Point to expose it. You may have one active identity at a time.
Action, spend 2 IP. Until the end of the scene, one equipped weapon deals Poison damage instead of its normal type. Gain +(SL) on checks related to poisons, venoms, and their detection or treatment.

Reaction to an incoming melee attack: roll an Accuracy Check as if attacking unarmed. If your result is higher than the attacker's, halve the damage. If lower, take double damage. If equal, execute a Perfect Parry — the attack is negated and you perform a free unarmed attack against the attacker.

Instead of dealing damage on a successful unarmed attack, make an opposed MIG+DEX vs MIG+MIG check. On success, set up the target: your next attack against them this scene deals × (1 + SL ÷ 3, rounded down) damage.
After hitting a target, mark them. Until the end of the scene, you gain +1 on all checks involving that target. The mark moves if the target flees or is replaced; you can only have one mark active.
While wearing no armour heavier than a padded jacket (no Martial armour), gain +1 die size on DEX checks to avoid damage or hazards. Gain +(SL) to checks to exit a hostile zone.

Action, spend (SL × 4) MP. Make a DEX + INS check. On success, execute a combination attack with one of the following effects (chosen before rolling): Finishing Blow (extra damage ×2); Fleet-Foot (attack + reposition without triggering reactions); Sweeping Strike (hits up to three targets in reach); Shoulder-Shaker (inflict Dazed); The Clinch (grapple — target cannot leave the scene until the end of the round).

When another player character acts from cowardice, cruelty, fear, or despair, they earn 1 FP as normal. You may then choose to sour or strengthen your Bond with them — whichever is honest — as a cost or reward for being right.

When a negative Bond emotion between two characters disappears after a genuine conversation, both characters earn 1 FP. You may spend 1 FP to trigger this once per scene if you facilitate the reconciliation.
Spend (SL × 5) MP to fill one extra clock segment when you (or an ally you are helping) defuse an NPC's anger, grief, or shame through genuine conversation.
On a melee attack against a target with at least one dark-trait marker, spend up to 5 MP. Deal (MP spent × SL) bonus light damage.
Reaction: when you or an adjacent ally would take damage from a target with at least one dark-trait marker, spend up to 10 MP. Reduce the damage by (MP spent × SL ÷ 2, rounded down).

Once per rest, ask one PC or significant NPC what they found attractive or admirable about you. Additionally, whenever you roll dice with a character who is currently Fond of you (has a positive Bond emotion toward you), you may reroll one of those dice once.
Write a list of your character's notable qualities (up to SL traits, chosen at creation or updated at level-up). When an NPC confirms they find one of those traits admirable, earn 1 FP.
Characters who help you gain +1 on their helping roll. Characters who attempt to harm or manipulate you also gain +1 on those rolls. Both bonuses apply to the same action when relevant.

Spend (SL × 5) MP. Until the end of the round, one creature of your choice must include you among its targets if it makes an area attack, or must target you if it makes a single-target attack. Alternatively, it may not target you at all — your choice, declared when you activate this.

Spend 10 MP. Add one emotion (positive or negative, your choice) to any Bond — including a Bond another character holds toward an NPC, or a Bond that does not yet exist (creating a temporary Bond for the scene). This emotion lasts until the end of the scene.

The aether saturating London's clay and chalk responds to your will. Move through solid earth, stone, or masonry without sound or trace, as current moves through a wire. At SL2, extend the passage to up to (WLP) willing companions. Cannot penetrate worked metal or timber framing.

Aether concentrated in substrata can be directed as elemental force — the industrial application of a phenomenon that only now has a name. Learn Elementalist spells; use INS + WLP for offensive checks. Each SL unlocks one additional spell (earth and stone formulae prioritised; other elements from SL4 onward). Elemental spells come only via this skill — there is no ritual-discipline route.

As a free action, spend 5 MP. Until the end of the scene, your body takes on the density of worked stone — aether saturating your musculature the way it saturates the substrata beneath London. You reduce all physical damage you take by 5.

Your eye reads the load-bearing lines before they fail — a shift in the aether-current through the stratum, a hairline in the keystone, the smell of wet clay under a dry floor. You are immune to environmental hazards from unstable ground (collapse, tremors, sinking foundations). Spend (SL × 5) MP to extend this protection to up to (SL) allies until the end of the scene.

You see the work that built this place: the aether-lines that hold it up, the point where one precise blow does what a hundred shouldn't. You always have access to basic masonry tools (chisel, mallet, iron spike, measuring line) without tracking them as inventory. When contributing to a clock related to structural construction or demolition, fill one additional segment.

Spend Acclaim to establish a combat Bond with one creature. For the scene, treat that Bond as a standard Bond for the purpose of skills that key on Bonds (e.g., Bond strength checks, Bond-keyed damage).
You have a network of admirers in each settlement you have performed in. They cover services (lodging, meals, basic equipment) up to a value of (SL + current Acclaim) × 30 zenit per rest.

Spend 10 MP. Make an opposed MIG + DEX vs MIG + MIG check against one creature in reach. On success, the creature cannot leave the scene until the end of your next turn. While grappled, you gain +(SL) on all checks against that creature.

Gain 1 Acclaim whenever you deal damage to a large or worse creature, take damage without being knocked out, or succeed on a check by 5 or more in a public setting. Spend Acclaim on Exhibition Bouts. Maximum (SL) Acclaim at once.

Spend Acclaim to execute a finisher: 1 Acclaim — Clash (weapon attack ×2 damage); 2 Acclaim — Whirlwind (attack all enemies in reach); 3 Acclaim — Pile Driver (attack + inflict Shaken); 4 Acclaim — Body Slam (attack + target cannot leave the scene for one round); 5 Acclaim — Showstopper (attack ×3 damage, all enemies in scene take 5 damage).

heroic_skills.display_name: A Bit of the Old Rough
heroic_skills.summary: ✎(printed: "Time for Ul-tra-vio-lence~" — a Clockwork Orange reference from 1962, renamed on the standing register rule; the new name is period slang and keeps the leer) Attack action with a melee brawling or spear weapon and nothing else equipped: make two separate attacks instead of one, at the same or different targets. Both follow two-weapon fighting — each loses the multi property and cannot gain it, and each treats High Roll as 0. If the first attack hits, that creature becomes broken until the start of your next turn: a broken creature takes extra damage equal to your Skill Level in Adrenaline, then stops being broken. ✎ Broken is a primed condition, not a seventh status, so no cleanse removes it — and it is private to this heroic: it never shares a trigger or a payout with reeling or ruptured. All that damage ignores Resistances, as printed. Does not stack with a custom weapon's quick customisation — still two attacks, not more. ⚠ Without Adrenaline the broken rider adds nothing; it is a Fury skill and the heroic does not require it.

After a creature performs an Accuracy or Magic Check for an attack or offensive spell that includes you among its targets — and you may decide after seeing the Result — spend 3 Inventory Points: you gain +20 Defense and Magic Defense until the end of that turn, and cannot use this again until the start of your next turn. +20 bought after seeing the roll is very nearly a guaranteed miss. The brake is the IP: 3 against a base of 6, at tenpence a point, so an Engineer who does this twice has spent their whole inventory and five shillings.
heroic_skills.requirements: Engineer (Tinkerer) mastery (the Merchant route is cut)

heroic_skills.summary: Once per scene, Cooking may combine four ingredients into one delicacy, ignoring the normal limit of three; everything else follows the normal rules. Four ingredients means up to six taste-pairs, which is where the six-effect line in the special rules comes from.

Choose two Species; against those or humanoid, either +5 damage or inflict reeling — a bespoke primed condition (the target's first recovery is halved, then it clears), not a seventh status, so no cleanse removes it. Takeable three times. Reeling is private to this heroic: it never shares a trigger or a payout with ruptured or broken.
heroic_skills.requirements: Fury, Archivist, Sharpshooter or Prizefighter mastery + Knowledge Is Power

heroic_skills.summary: Entering the Panoply, spend 1 Fabula Point to invoke your Theme: +5 entry damage, and until the form ends — Immunity to your element; your element's damage-bypass clause works as printed; and once per Check, 10 MP to reroll either or both dice, non-fumble. Once per rest. The Immunity stands, ruled as the campaign's one sanctioned transcendent state: unlike Pulse of the Maggots it is once per rest, Theme-invoked, Fabula-priced and form-scoped — a climax, not a statblock.

When you hit one or more creatures with an arcane weapon, the attack deals 5 extra damage and you may choose one of them: if the next offensive spell you cast this scene targets only that creature, its Magic Check critically succeeds on any matching pair, provided it is not a fumble.

Once per scene, when you and/or allies would drop to 0 HP, all of them go to exactly 1 instead; you immediately dismiss your merged Arcanum. The one stay-up effect that never ticks Miasma — it stops the fall rather than reversing it.

When you merge with an Arcanum, use Symbolism for free (paying the IP). And on a pulse or willing dismiss, spend 1 IP to change one symbol on a visible creature to another you know. No free symbol on a Quick Summoning merge.
After an enemy costs you HP with an attack, spell or Skill while you are merged: deal 5 damage back, physical or of a type your Arcanum grants you Resistance to, after their action resolves.
Memorise the High Roll of an examination Check; spend it later to add or subtract that much damage. Discovery converted into damage, literally.

After an enemy you can see hits or misses you with an offensive spell, if the Result of their Magic Check was even, you may immediately use Invocation for free — after the spell fully resolves — against that enemy, spending no Mind Points. The invocation must not be a hex, may target only that enemy, and cannot use Linked Invocation. A reaction with a named trigger, a coin-flip gate and a target restriction; it passes the free-action rule without argument.
heroic_skills.requirements: Dowser (Invoker), Elementalist, Entropist or Symbolist mastery + Invocation

heroic_skills.summary: When you resolve Double Trouble you may make all its damage light or dark instead of matching the resolved suits — the second effect in the class that reaches outside the four elements. And while a joker sits in your discard pile, Blinding Flush, Double Trouble and Magic Flush damage ignores Immunities and Resistances, as printed. Standard treatment, same as Numen, Hunter's Instinct, Fabula Impetum and Revenant.
heroic_skills.requirements: Cartomancer (Ace of Cards), Blackguard (Darkblade), Entropist or Spiritist mastery

heroic_skills.summary: Where rest costs at least 10 zenit, you have access to at least one shop connected to a secret network, selling up to three items priced up to 500 zenit above your party's suggested maximum item value. The rest-cost gate is a wealth gate, and here a geography gate: ten-zenit lodging is the West End and the coaching inns, so the black market is uptown. Houndsditch trades in what was stolen; this trades in what was imported. It never sells hoplospheres — the jeweller's window is the sanctioned channel, and a criminal channel that could order spheres would break "you cannot buy the one you need".

With one or more melee dagger weapons equipped: +1 Defense and Magic Defense, and those weapons also count as brawling, sword and thrown for the purpose of Skills and effects. Your dagger-Category attacks may also target creatures melee cannot normally reach.
heroic_skills.requirements: Rogue, Prizefighter (Weaponmaster) or Bounty Hunter mastery

heroic_skills.summary: When you perform a Ritual you cannot fully afford, pay part of its Mind Point cost with Hit Points at 2 HP per 1 MP — never down to 0 HP. A Ritual paid for this way heals neither you nor any ally who supported its Magic Check (it works normally on any other target). Vismagus may be part-paid the same way, its other restrictions intact.
heroic_skills.requirements: Butcher, Blackguard (Darkblade) or Mutant mastery + Vismagus

heroic_skills.summary: While your Brainwave Clock is full, use an action to erase all of its sections and choose: 20 physical damage to every enemy in the scene, or 30 to a single enemy you can see. Increases by 10 at level 20+, or 20 at level 40+. This is the only way to clear the Clock.

You are Resistant to light and poison damage. After you lose Hit Points, if you are in Crisis and a magiseed is in your garden, you may fill 1 section of your Growth Clock. And Shadow Strike may deal poison instead of dark (the type still cannot be changed), dealing extra damage equal to twice your filled sections. The third clause needs the Blackguard; the first two work on a pure Floralist, and the Crisis clause is one of the two sanctioned ways to fill the clock off-schedule.

When Bone Crusher targets only one creature and you have a shield equipped, challenge that creature until the end of your next turn: it must include you among the targets of its attacks and offensive spells, if able. Once per turn — including other creatures' turns — you deal 5 extra damage to it with a free attack using a one-handed melee weapon, or a custom dagger or sword. The challenge ends if someone else challenges it, or if you challenge another.
heroic_skills.requirements: Captain (Commander), Fury, Guardian, Prizefighter (Weaponmaster) or Bounty Hunter mastery + Bone Crusher (the Pilot route is cut)

heroic_skills.summary: When applying a symbol to yourself or an ally, spend up to 30 MP: every 10 MP copies it onto another ally you can see (each copy counts against your limit). Symbolism's free attack gains multi (2).

After an enemy's Accuracy or Magic Check, grant it +3 to the Result; in exchange you and every ally who can hear you gain Resistance to all damage types until end of turn, or deal +5 damage. Kept as printed — a bought moment, not an ambient blanket.

You learn the class's ultimate spell: Calamity, 40 MP, one creature, instantaneous — the target suffers dazed, enraged, poisoned, shaken, slow and weak, all six at once. Under house rules that also steps every one of its attributes down, floor d6, so its Defense and Magic Defense fall with them.

When you discard for Magic Cards, you may set 1 of those cards face down in front of you as a vanguard card instead of discarding it — maximum 2 in play. When any source damages you and/or allies you can see, reveal one: if it is a joker or its suit matches that damage type, you and every ally you can see gain Resistance to that type until the end of the turn, and the card goes on top of the discard pile. You may look at your own vanguard cards whenever you like; any still in play at the end of a conflict shuffle back into the deck.

Choose a weapon Category: +2 Accuracy and +5 damage with it. Not a Guise Perk — no heroic is. A brawler mask grants the permission to fight like the thing it came off; this is the character learning to, and it keeps working unmasked.
The MP costs of Bishop's Edict, Charging Cavalry and King's Castle are halved — 10 MP becomes 5. The purest heroic in the class: it does nothing except let you do the thing twice as often.

Use an action and spend up to 30 MP, choosing one creature you can see per 5 MP spent, up to six. Each recovers from all status effects and is no longer affected by any spell with a duration of Scene. Six-target full cleanse for 30 MP — and it strips the party's own Scene-duration buffs too. The single best answer on the roster to the Apothecary's multi-type Affliction.

At any moment, with at least 4 active Motes, spend 40 MP to imbue one equipped weapon with them: until the effect ends the weapon gains +3 to Accuracy Checks, and its damage ignores Resistances. The Motes used are destroyed. A melee weapon also becomes ranged, launchable from afar. If you had the weapon equipped while casting, perform a free attack with it as part of the same action. You generate Motes as normal from the next turn onwards. Only one weapon at a time. (Low Fantasy Atlas p.107, verified 10 Aug 2026.)
heroic_skills.requirements: No Requirements line printed (Low Fantasy Atlas p.107, The Prestige precedent) — Adept mastery inferred, in line with every other class heroic; the working prerequisite is in the text: at least 4 active Motes

heroic_skills.summary: Action: choose one creature suffering Affliction and another two targets you can see — three if you also have Infectious. Each suffers Affliction including every damage type the original carries; a target that already has it gains only the types it lacked. Against a group this is the largest single play the class has.

Outside a conflict, spend 3 Reputation Points and choose a crowd of non-hostile humanoids able to hear and understand you: they are swayed by your voice and follow your commands for the rest of the scene, against even their own better judgement. It ends when the crowd disperses, and for anyone who leaves it. Using this ticks the Miasma Clock by 1 — in 1892 London it is mob incitement, and a crowd acting against its own better judgement is precisely the input the Clock exists to measure.
When Shadow Strike's HP loss does not drop you to 0, every ally present recovers (the HP you lost + your SL in Shadow Strike) — +10 at level 30+. The self-harm engine, made generous.

At conflict start, choose an ally you hold a strength-3 Bond toward: you two are connected for the scene, and may pay each other's MP costs for spells, Skills and effects (never rituals). One connection per creature; it ends if either leaves, falls, or the Bond drops below 3.
You reduce Inventory Point costs by 1, to a minimum of 1. Level-up only. On the standing watch list as a p.266 offender among non-Guise effects.
Advanced and superior potions ignore Resistances.

Attacking with a bow and no other weapon equipped, make two separate attacks instead of one, at the same or different targets. Both follow two-weapon fighting: each loses the multi property and cannot gain it, and each treats High Roll as 0. Does not stack with a custom weapon's quick customisation.

Inventory action + 3 IP: consume an alcoholic drink and become drunk. While drunk your Dexterity counts as one die size higher, to a maximum of d12, and when an enemy misses you, you deal damage equal to your current Dexterity die — physical, or the type a dance changed your damage to. It ends at the end of the scene, if you die or fall unconscious, if you take a potion or delicacy that clears a status, or if you are Cleansed. How you play it is yours to choose: genuinely drunk, or a fighter affecting drunkenness to make himself hard to read. The mechanics are identical and the table does not have to agree. The die raise obeys the standing rule — raises never stack, d12 is the ceiling.
heroic_skills.requirements: Dancer, Fury, Cook (Gourmet) or Traveller (Wayfarer) mastery

heroic_skills.summary: When you resolve Magic Pair, if the free attack uses an arcane, dagger, firearm, sword or thrown weapon, you deal extra damage equal to the pair's common value and recover twice that value in MP. The MP return is the point: Magic Cards costs at least 10 MP a use, so a Duel Master resolving pairs runs close to cost-neutral on the engine. It stacks with Double or Nothing, which touches the attack's High Roll and never the pair's value.
heroic_skills.requirements: Cartomancer (Ace of Cards), Fury, Rogue, Sharpshooter or Prizefighter (Weaponmaster) mastery

heroic_skills.summary: You always know the Species of creatures you can see. When preparing a delicacy in a conflict, treat visible enemies as ingredients (harmlessly; once per enemy per scene) — bitter plant, salty construct, sour demon, sweet undead, umami elemental, monsters any taste. Beasts and humanoids aren't strange enough, apparently. Resting a travel day from any settlement grants bonus ingredients.

Once per staged adventure, when you complete a stage, ask the GM a question or name something you wish to know; they must give a complete answer, or hand you 1 Fabula Point if it cannot be known or deduced. ✎ The printed Five Stage Dungeon is answered by declaration rather than by importing Spelunca Ultima: Entrance is getting into the house, Puzzle the cipher or the séance, Setback the thing going wrong, Conflict the confrontation, Reward the aftermath. ⚠ The list of qualifying adventures must be named and visible to the player before this is bought, or the heroic is a coin-flip on the GM's mood.

You learn the forbidden poison spell: 20 MP, one creature, (HR + 30) poison damage that ignores Resistances; poisoned on HR 8+, or automatically with Pathogenesis. The closest thing in print to weaponised Miasma — the Cabal's signature shape.
On a successful Check to fill or erase Clock sections, deal 5 damage of a chosen type per section to all enemies in the scene. Fires on Pressure Clocks — staggering becomes a group-damage engine.
When a creature first enters Crisis in a scene you are in, immediately perform the Inventory action to create and use a consumable on them. Ruled once per scene.

+2 Bond slots; you may instantly create a Bond with one emotion; all your Bonds count 1 point stronger (inert if another effect already holds you at 4+). Near-default here — Bonds are Status, and the printed text already refuses to stack with the resolved-Tell +1.
Your Life Well loses only half its stored HP when you finish a rest, instead of all of it.
Permanently increase your maximum Hit Points by 10 — 20 at level 40 or higher. Level-up only: a flat boost that belongs to the person, never the mask.
Permanently increase your maximum Inventory Points by 4. Level-up only: a flat boost that belongs to the person, never the mask.
Permanently increase your maximum Mind Points by 10 — 20 at level 40 or higher. Level-up only: a flat boost that belongs to the person, never the mask.

Learn two more tools from the Hunter's Tools list — a maxed kit goes from 10 of 28 to 12 — and every tool with a target of "Self" now targets "Yourself or an ally". That second clause is the real heroic: Steel Skin, Immune System Enhancer, Immunity Serum, Stimulant and Medpack all become things you hand to somebody else. It does not combine with Army of One — Extra Tools changes who you may target, Army of One changes how many, and they stay separate.
