Adrenaline Shot works as printed on yourself or, through this, an ally: the Crisis it manufactures is real for everything keyed to Crisis status (F10). Carve-outs are per-effect, only where Crisis at full health would be degenerate — Into the Otherworld is gated on actual current HP, and is so far the only one.

Once per scene, you may use an action and spend up to 2 Fabula Points to perform a free attack with a weapon you have equipped. For each Fabula Point spent this way, that attack gains +2 to its Accuracy Check and deals 10 extra damage. All damage dealt by this attack becomes light and its type cannot change. Damage dealt by this attack against Villains ignores Immunities and Resistances, as printed. It is light damage and it is NOT a bane: banes are materials, they pass only through physical objects, and no spell or Fabula-Point effect produces one. Very good against undead and anything light-Vulnerable — not a free silver bullet.
heroic_skills.requirements: Stalwart (Hero) mastery — "You must have mastered the Hero Class" (Hero_Class.pdf, verified 10 Aug 2026)

heroic_skills.summary: Temporarily acquire another PC's spell or Skill for a scene — Heroic Skills explicitly included — at SL1, with none of the attached benefits. The one learn-from-others mechanic that copies from your friends.

A Ritual creating a permanent fey crossing at your location: (INS + WLP), 80 MP, Difficulty 13, Major/Small, usable thereafter with Fey Crossing. Backfire: "you attract the attention of something greater than yourself." Your gates are safer than wild ones but not safe — they draw other fey. Requires the Rituals benefit-pool pick; Guises grant no ritual access. At 80 MP against a level-30 pool of roughly 90 it is very nearly everything you have, which is right for a door between worlds. Treat the Backfire as a real hook: it names no creature and no consequence, which makes a failed Fey Gate a district-level event.
heroic_skills.requirements: Cunning Folk mastery + Fey Crossing (and the Rituals benefit-pool pick)

heroic_skills.summary: Adds two dances, both keyed to the Fencer's Stances. Crane Dance: recover 3 HP or MP when a creature misses you; both while in Parry Stance. Viper Dance: gain Resistance to poison, or convert your damage to poison; doubles on an Accuracy or Magic Check while in Lunge Stance inflict poisoned. Reachable through Dancer mastery alone — the Stance clauses only pay off if the character is also a Fencer.

After discarding via Magic Cards, if the set held a joker: shuffle any non-joker discards back into the deck. Adds the Forbidden Monarch set — four of a kind plus a joker: 777 damage to every enemy you can see, light if the value is even, dark if odd. The joker-in-discard Immunity/Resistance bypass is struck per the standing rule; the 777 stays (ruled: the epic draw is a hype moment).
heroic_skills.requirements: Cartomancer or Arcanist mastery + Magic Cards SL3

heroic_skills.summary: After a successful Provoke, Provoke again free (and again, while you keep succeeding on enemies not yet tried this turn). When an enraged enemy hits you with an attack or offensive spell, recover 5 MP.

Action: grab a willing visible ally and throw them — an Open (DEX+MIG) or (MIG+INS) Check (crits on doubles with Frenzy); the ally makes a free attack dealing extra damage equal to the Open Check's result, inflicting weak on each creature hit. On a fumble or miss the ally takes your Might die size in physical.
heroic_skills.requirements: Dancer, Fury or Mutant mastery (the Pilot route is cut)

heroic_skills.summary: When you cast Drain Spirit or Drain Vigor you recover the full MP or HP the target lost instead of half, and Drain Spirit's MP loss increases by 5 at level 20+ and by 10 at level 40+. This is an Entropist skill with the Reaper bolted on: both Drain spells are Entropist spells and the Reaper's own list contains neither, so a single-class Reaper cannot use it — what survives for them alone is Raising. Say it at build time.
heroic_skills.requirements: Entropist or Reaper (Necromancer) mastery + both the Drain Spirit and Drain Vigor spells

heroic_skills.summary: Treat the alchemy target die as 13 or 17.

A benefit keyed to your unarmed strikes' current Category, and multiple Categories stack their benefits: arcane, brawling, dagger or thrown reads target Defense off their Insight die · bow or sword adds 5 damage on multi-target attacks · firearm or heavy adds 5 against constructs and the shield-and-armour-clad · flail or spear grants +2 Defense and reach into the air.

Once per turn, when a magiseed leaves your garden, if it has one or more "at the end of your turn" effects, spend 20 MP to reproduce one of them — including an effect that does not match your current filled sections. And with Verdant Sway, your Rituals may influence and control soldier-Rank plant-Species creatures; never create them. Read the first clause against Wrathful Carnation: voluntary removal is a magiseed leaving your garden, and so is Graft. This is how a Floralist fires a tier-3 effect from a clock sitting at 1.
Ecdysis may also clear all status effects and/or end every Scene-duration spell on you.
Rewritten by the adopted variant: three forms, and the free attack keeps its full High Roll. See the class's house changes for the form list and the flight rule.

When you fill 1 or more sections of your Growth Clock, either fill 1 additional section or fill 1 fewer, to a minimum of 0 — then you cannot use this again until the Clock is completely empty. The magiseed damage clause ignores Resistances, as printed, and it reaches only the five seeds that deal damage themselves (Grave Asphodel, Serrated Rose, Star Peony, Striped Orchid, Wardwattle). The accelerator half is untouched and is the whole reason to take the skill — "1 fewer" is how you hold a tier-3 effect for a second turn.

Follow My Lead works on any visible ally, Bonds regardless — and on a lasting dance (not Hydra) may extend the effect to every ally you can see. When allies under your Resistance-granting dance or verse take that very type, end the effect on them to grant Immunity to it until end of turn.
When you roll a critical success on an Accuracy Check, you or a creature of your choice regains 1 Inventory Point. Straight into the Bane Oils economy.
Battle Gardening may swap its free attack or spell for one of: a free Study at +(SL in Battle Gardening); or a free Inventory action that must create an elixir, remedy or tonic.

Choose a status at acquisition (dazed/shaken/slow/weak). After an ally's damage costs enemies HP and at least one was Vulnerable to it, one of them loses (half your level + twice your best of Cheap Shot / Personal Vehicle) HP and suffers the status. Once per round, party-wide.
heroic_skills.requirements: Rogue mastery (the Pilot route is cut) + Cheap Shot or the Personal Vehicle pool pick

heroic_skills.summary: With a weapon in your main hand and a shield in your off-hand, that weapon's attacks deal 5 extra damage and you gain +1 Defense. Cannot combine with a custom weapon's defence-boost customisation, nor with Dual Shieldbearer.

Choose two Attributes for non-martial weapon Accuracy; a basic staff counts as brawling, heavy, spear and sword and deals +10; improvised weapons deal +5 and may survive the attack. The gentleman's walking-stick.

Three clauses. With Lockdown and Condemn, you may use Lockdown when you successfully Condemn a creature. When you Encourage an ally, you may apply a bane oil to a weapon they have equipped as part of the same action (still paying the 2 IP). And when you Encourage an ally, you may use Know Thy Quarry for that ally's Checks until the start of your next turn.
heroic_skills.requirements: Slayer AND Orator mastery — both, not either

heroic_skills.summary: After you roll a Check, spend 1 Fabula Point to invoke your Bounty as an Instinct: that Check triggers a critical success if both dice show the same number, provided the Result is not a fumble. And damage dealt by your tools ignores Immunities and Resistances against your Bounty, as printed. Tools cost 2–4 IP and IP is finite, so this is realistically 3–5 tools a conflict — preparation pays, and against your Bounty it pays through.

When you transform a transforming custom weapon on your turn, choose one: if you have performed no attacks this turn, your next attack with that weapon this turn deals 5 extra damage; or if you have already hit one or more creatures with it this turn, recover 5 HP and 5 MP. A small, honest reward for using the transformation rather than picking a form and staying in it.

When you use Shadow Strike you may treat your High Roll as 0 when determining that attack's damage. If you do, once Shadow Strike's effects resolve, you may immediately perform Charging Cavalry for free — paying its MP cost as normal. Live: it was filed as a dead letter solely because Commander was believed to be out of the lineup.
heroic_skills.requirements: Captain (Commander) or Blackguard (Darkblade) mastery + Charging Cavalry and Shadow Strike

heroic_skills.summary: When you use Fleshcraft on an NPC, the GM must reveal every spell it knows. If it knows one or more, you may learn one of them as a Chimerist spell of your own — even if that NPC's Species is not among those Spell Mimic normally allows.
heroic_skills.requirements: Butcher or Vivisectionist (Chimerist) mastery + Fleshcraft and Spell Mimic

heroic_skills.summary: Withstand may raise any Attribute (not just MIG/WLP), and also recovers (5 + SL in Withstand × your highest Bond strength) MP on top of the HP. Your first damage before your next turn ends deals +(SL in Withstand).

On acquisition and at every rest, choose one wellspring — air, earth, fire, lightning or water. Until your next rest you always treat it as available in every scene on top of whatever the GM named; you may perform Elementalism Rituals manipulating that element; you gain Resistance to its damage type; and you may change your damage to its type. The change-type clause also ignores Resistances, as printed. ⚠ The audit missed this clause entirely, working from the summary table. Note also that a second ritual discipline is contested at one per party: a Dowser taking this claims Elementalism for the table.

Turns your Unexpected Ally into a follower — a persistent group asset on the GM's-Booklet NPC rules. The biggest upgrade any benefit-pool pick receives; a creation choice becomes a standing member of the Lodge.
The first potion you make each scene costs 0 IP. (The name is period-solid and stays — 1892 is the golden age of industrial life assurance.)

While that low: action + 40 MP overlays a pocket dimension reflecting your psyche, containing any creatures you choose. A 4-segment Otherworld Clock erases each turn (and on damage with a WLP roll of 3 or lower). Inside, one chosen spell or free-attack Skill automatically succeeds at HR 5, and one Attribute runs a size larger (max d12). The Unmasking, made literal.

After hitting with a melee spear and no other weapon equipped, spend 20 MP and choose one creature you hit. The attack deals half damage to all of its targets, and you choose an action type — Attack, Guard, Objective, Spell or Skill. From then on that creature must spend 10 MP to perform that action type, or perform a different one instead; lasts until the start of your next turn or until you use it again. An action tax on one enemy, bought by halving the hit that applied it: very good against a Villain with one answer, 20 MP for a nuisance against anything with options.
heroic_skills.requirements: Captain (Commander), Prizefighter (Weaponmaster) or Bounty Hunter mastery

heroic_skills.summary: Inventory action: throw a material or rare item you own at a visible creature for (its value ÷ 50) damage, typed by the item's nature (else physical). Then d6: 1 destroys it, 2–3 damages it (destroyed if thrown again; unusable until repaired), 4–6 no harm.
heroic_skills.requirements: Cook, Rogue or Engineer mastery (the Merchant route is cut)

heroic_skills.summary: When you prepare a delicacy you may take a portion of leftovers — a special ingredient carrying all the tastes used in it, which spoils at the end of the scene. Using leftovers, choose one of its tastes; it counts as an ingredient of that taste only. No leftovers from a delicacy made with leftovers, and one portion at a time.
heroic_skills.requirements: Butcher or Cook (Gourmet) mastery + Cooking and Waste Not

heroic_skills.summary: On acquisition, name the Villain you brought down or brought back. You gain an extra Bond slot and a Bond toward them, emotions discussed with the group — then, together with the group, you create and acquire that Villain's Legacy: something your character learned from what they did. One of their iconic moves, a piece of rare equipment, or a whole new Skill. The Legacy is designed at the table, so it is only as balanced as the table makes it; agree its shape before it is written down. Source is unplaytested by its own admission.
heroic_skills.requirements: You must have been responsible for a Villain's redemption or demise

heroic_skills.summary: Once per conflict, after Studying, gain Resistance to two non-physical damage types for the scene. Pays for the action the pressure game already wants taken.
Cooking's free attack, on a delicacy of at most 2 ingredients: gains multi (2), and if the delicacy has no damaging effects, +5 damage.

After a successful Soul Steal: one target is Studied for free, immediately, using the Soul Steal Check's own Result and High Roll — no dice. And you deal +(SL in Soul Steal) damage to an elite or champion whose soul treasure you stole this scene. The sphere comes out and you learn what it was, one motion.
heroic_skills.requirements: Sensitive, Archivist or Rogue mastery + Soul Steal

heroic_skills.summary: When a potion or delicacy you create heals allies, you recover half that value yourself.

CAPPED — choose ONE category when you take it; the choice is permanent. Printed, all your spells gain an extra effect forever across six categories: multi-target spells cost 10 MP less · damaging spells +10 damage (+15 at 20, +20 at 40) · healing +10 HP (+15 at 20, +20 at 40) · negative-status spells also apply enraged or poisoned · positive-status spells also apply one of dex-up, mig-up, wlp-up or ins-up · resource-draining spells double what they gain. The source's own limiter: a spell qualifying for two categories uses one, chosen per casting. Uncapped this is the largest heroic in the collection — always on, every spell, for the rest of the campaign — so mastery-gating alone is not enough. Note it does not require Cunning Folk: a mastered Spiritist or Elementalist can hold it having never touched the class.
heroic_skills.requirements: Cunning Folk, Spiritist or Elementalist mastery

heroic_skills.summary: Before you cast a malediction, double its HP cost to alter one of its lifting conditions. The counterplay tax, priced correctly: every malediction's balance sits in its lifting condition, and this buys the right to move one at double the blood. Watch it against Entangle — three targets is 30 HP printed, 60 amended — and rule that "alter" means rewrite, not delete, with a replacement the targets can actually attempt. Say it before it is used, not after.

Swords join Frenzy's crit list. With a two-handed sword equipped: spend an Opportunity for a free attack, +5 damage, generating no Opportunities (once per round). And when your two-handed sword costs creatures HP: spend 1 Fabula Point to reduce one non-Villain among them, whose HP are at or under your Crisis score, to 0.
heroic_skills.requirements: Fury or Prizefighter mastery (the Pilot route is cut)

heroic_skills.summary: When you use your action for Exploit, spend an extra 10 MP to aim it at one creature and exploit every status on it at once. At the start of each of your later turns this conflict that target takes (SL × its number of status effects) damage, of the type of one of your equipped weapons — physical if you have none. It counts as your one exploited status; later you may return to exploiting normally with an action, or spend 10 MP to move it to a new target. With Calamity this is the capstone combination: six statuses billed every turn, automatic, no roll. A legitimate capstone rather than a loophole — but against an elite it is a delete button, and your Villains want their Ultima Points in hand before it lands.

6 IP: one creature permanently gains +10 maximum HP or +10 maximum MP, or +5 of each, the target's choice — once per creature ever. Restored 5 Aug under the derived-stat rule: the gain attaches to the Guise the recipient is wearing when dosed, not to the body. Dose the coat, not the man — hand that Guise on and the +10 goes with it, while an Innate-only character takes it into the frame they can never remove. "Once per creature" reads once per Guise, once per Innate frame.

You gain an additional free use of an organisational ability as part of your Incorporate Skill. The book contradicts itself: its summary table reads "choose two additional organisational abilities", the full entry two pages later reads "an additional free use". The full entry is the prose one and is the one to use — one more free activation, not two more abilities on the menu.

At the start of a conflict involving at least one Villain, name one of them your Nemesis until they leave the scene or it ends. At the start of your turn you may recover HP equal to (their maximum Ultima Points minus their current Ultima Points). Whenever your Nemesis spends an Ultima Point you gain 1 Nemesis Point, spendable in place of a Fabula Point when invoking a trait or a Bond — and that counts as having spent a Fabula Point for anything that checks. Nemesis Points never count toward Experience, and any unspent are lost at the end of the scene. Source is unplaytested by its own admission.
heroic_skills.requirements: You must have witnessed a Villain Ascension

heroic_skills.summary: Shadow Strike becomes fire or ice and grants Resistance to the other; its free melee attack can reach otherwise-untargetable enemies.
heroic_skills.requirements: Blackguard or Elementalist mastery + Shadow Strike (the Pilot route is cut)

heroic_skills.summary: Apply the effects of Arming Maneuver, Hero's Right Hand and Team Player to your cognitive focus, as long as you hold a Bond with them and can hear each other. Team Player travels in its house form — the blanket-Resistance clause stripped from it stays stripped here. Live: the dead-letter reading assumed the Sensitive was out of the lineup, and it is not.

Once per encounter, when you are in Crisis after taking damage, note the type of the triggering damage: you have Resistance to that type until the end of the encounter. Damage with no type cannot trigger it. Ruled in against the affinity rule — conditional, reactive and temporary, on a par with the Resistances spells already grant. You cannot choose the type; the enemy chooses it by hitting you with it.

Heart of Darkness may now create a Bond of hatred or inferiority, or strengthen an existing Bond whose only emotion is one of those. When you damage a creature you hold hatred and/or inferiority toward, you deal additional damage equal to your Bond strength with it.
In the Panoply, when a creature you hold an admiration, loyalty or affection Bond toward spends MP on a spell or ritual, pay up to (Bond strength × 10) of it for them. One patron per casting.
heroic_skills.requirements: Sensitive (Esper), Penny Knight or Spiritist mastery

heroic_skills.summary: Empty Mind becomes a d10 instead of a fixed exit: 1 exits your Stance · 2–5 enters Lunge Stance · 6–9 enters Parry Stance · 10 remains, and on your next turn you lose all Tempo and enter Virtuose Stance. The 10 converts any amount of Tempo into Virtuose Stance, which makes this the class's accelerator as much as its gamble.
heroic_skills.requirements: Fencer mastery + Empty Mind + two Stance skills

heroic_skills.summary: After applying a symbol in a conflict, pick a target that was already bearing one of yours: it performs a free attack (basic for NPCs), or recovers 10 MP, or suffers dazed, or suffers slow.
While you are in Crisis, Follow My Lead costs no MP. A one-line heroic that turns the class's most expensive rider free at exactly the moment the party is losing.
Peacock Dance may instead read: choose a creature that can see you and suffers one or more statuses — it must include you among its attack and offensive-spell targets until your next turn, if able.

CAPPED to out-of-conflict recovery. Printed: recover 5 HP per turn while in heavy shadows or darkness, or every few minutes outside a conflict. In most settings that condition is a real one; here it is the default lighting — London fog, gaslight, night work, cellars, the Underground works, and a doctrine that Rippers fight out of public view. Uncapped it is a mastery heroic granting permanent regeneration. Capped, the vampire is simply the one who is fine after a bad night. (The alternative cap is once per scene; either works.)

While you have at least 4 active Motes: +1 to Defense, Magic Defense and Accuracy Checks. Motes arrive 2 a round against a cap of 6, so "at least 4" is your default state rather than a hurdle. The +1 Accuracy counts toward p.266's two-effect cap among non-Guise effects — Guise bonuses sit outside it.

Spend 1 Tempo for +2 on a Study or Objective Check; gain 2 Tempo when you enter Virtuose Stance; spend 3 Tempo to advance a Growth Clock one extra time. Objective actions fill Pressure Clocks, so this makes the Fencer a second pressure enabler alongside the Antiquarian. The Growth Clock clause only matters if the character is also a Floralist — and it is the only cross-class lever on that clock in the lineup.
heroic_skills.requirements: Fencer, Floralist or Archivist (Loremaster) mastery + Virtuose Stance

heroic_skills.summary: Dispel becomes 10×T on up to three creatures; when you end scene-duration spells on enemies, recover 20 MP per spell or copy each onto yourself. Theft rather than mimicry, and the enemy has to have buffed first.
heroic_skills.requirements: Vivisectionist, Entropist, Cook or Mutant mastery

heroic_skills.summary: Symbolism may spend +5 MP to make the symbol artistic. When you cast a spell, recover (2 × artistic symbols in the scene) HP. When an artistic symbol is destroyed, a creature you choose recovers your WLP die size in MP.

Cataclysm ignores Resistances as printed, and where it already did so, Immunities as well — the escalation tier has a real bypass to escalate from again. ⚠ Watch-listed: allowed as printed on 15 Aug, to be revisited if it bites in play.

Dark, earth, ice or physical damage earns a Yin Point; air, bolt, fire or light a Yang Point; +5 damage while holding one of the other kind. At 3+ with one of each, spend all to drain MP from every enemy or restore an ally's. Rewards alternating damage types — nothing else does.
heroic_skills.requirements: Dancer, Elementalist, Sensitive or Dowser mastery

heroic_skills.summary: After a successful Soul Steal against one or more enemies, choose one and immediately use Amputate against it, treating that Check's Result and High Roll as equal to the Soul Steal Check's — no roll. And when you steal an enemy's soul treasure you recover MP equal to (4 × your Skill Level in Soul Steal).
heroic_skills.requirements: Butcher or Rogue mastery + Amputate and Soul Steal

heroic_skills.summary: Your ranged attacks deal 5 extra damage — 10 at level 40 or higher. Level-up only.
Spells you cast deal 5 extra damage — 10 at level 40 or higher. Level-up only.
heroic_skills.requirements: Vivisectionist (Chimerist), Elementalist, Entropist or Spiritist mastery

heroic_skills.summary: Your melee attacks deal 5 extra damage — 10 at level 40 or higher. Level-up only.

Take the place of all allies threatened by one danger, resolving it separately for each; and a permanent maximum-HP increase equal to your base Insight die. ✎ RESERVED FOR THE LEVEL 40 AND 50 SLOTS (ruled 7 Aug): the rider is a permanent stat gain sized off a die, which makes its arithmetic sit oddly against everything else on the sheet. Held to the endgame slots rather than amended, so the printed effect survives intact.
heroic_skills.requirements: Entropist or Guardian mastery — ✎ and only in a level 40 or 50 slot

heroic_skills.summary: When you hit with a melee attack, you may cover an ally as though you had taken the Guard action. None of Guard's other benefits apply.

Up to once per conflict, when you or an ally you hold a Bond of affection, admiration or loyalty toward is targeted by a Villain's attack, spell or special rule, spend 1 Fabula Point: you and that ally avoid all of its damage, and its consequences do not apply to you. Describe how. "Consequences" means the action's own secondary effects — status effects, MP loss, and any Clock that action would move. It is a shield against the blow, not an eraser of story: what the Villain did still happened and everyone present still saw it. The Villain's entrance already ticked the Miasma Clock once for the whole of their conduct, so there is normally no exposure tick to block — except in a conflict that makes public exposure its own mechanic, which is exactly the case this is worth spending a Fabula Point on. Source is unplaytested by its own admission.
heroic_skills.requirements: You must have surrendered to a Villain and suffered a dire consequence

heroic_skills.summary: While you have no martial armor and no shield equipped, all damage is reduced by (1 + filled Brainwave sections), before Affinities. A choice that costs an armour slot — the Innate Guise may wear ordinary purchased armour.

Your weapons count as arcane. With a full Brainwave Clock, choose at end of turn: party cleanse of dazed/enraged/shaken; party 5 HP and 5 MP; mass dazed + shaken; mass enraged; or the GM reveals your cognitive focus's Affinities.

On Guard (if you did not Guard last turn), choose ranged attacks or offensive spells; until your next turn: Counterattack triggers on all melee hits and misses regardless of parity, its free attacks deal +5 when the trigger hit you, and it also triggers on your chosen category. The heroic that must never ride a Guise distilled from something that ran.

As long as your personal vehicle has a steed frame, it may have up to 2 active weapon modules instead of 1. During a conflict, if you have a martial armor equipped, you may use an action and spend 30 Mind Points to choose earth or physical: you deal 20 damage of the chosen type to every enemy you can see, and enemies that lose Hit Points this way cannot perform free attacks until the start of their next turn. +10 damage if you are driving a personal vehicle with a mech frame and/or have two shields equipped; +10 more at level 30 or higher. (June 2026 playtest materials p.17, verified 10 Aug 2026.)
heroic_skills.requirements: Guardian mastery (printed: "Guardian or Pilot" — Pilot is cut); the vehicle clauses ride the Personal Vehicle benefit pick

heroic_skills.summary: With a non-martial, melee, two-handed brawling weapon: +5 damage, may target flying creatures, counts as spear and sword for Category-gated Skills, and may attack twice under two-weapon rules (forfeiting the +5 on each). In 1892: a quarterstaff, singlestick, cudgel or cane.
When you Study during a conflict, examine the profiles of every enemy you can see: one (INS + INS) Open Check, applied separately to each. If you have Flash of Insight, this Check cannot trigger it.

The NPC must die where you can see it; you cannot raise a corpse you found. Raise a non-Villain NPC of the beast, monster or plant Species as a minion, for 2 Grave Points and a reduction to your maximum HP and MP equal to its level. Its Species becomes undead and the new dark/light/poison Affinities overwrite any it had; Rank becomes soldier with Skills kept; it arrives at full HP and MP with its original equipment; it takes its own turn on telepathic command and the GM counts it as an additional PC when designing conflicts; it rests when you rest. You lose it at 0 HP, more than one travel day away, if you die or fall unconscious, or if you destroy it — and the reduction ends with it. One at a time. HOUSE RESTRICTION: beast, monster and plant only, never humanoid — a player who wants that version gets a story event with the Miasma Clock and the Medjay both responding, not a heroic they own. The cost rides the Guise that raised the minion; stash the Guise and the minion goes inert with the reduction suspended.

When a rule or ability requires you to spend a Fabula Point, you may instead choose a Bond and replace an emotion of Admiration, Affection or Loyalty with one of Inferiority, Mistrust or Hatred — and ignore that cost. A second route to paying costs in something other than the intended currency, and it reaches any Fabula Point cost rather than just spells. Self-limiting only while the character has positive emotions left to spend.
When your energetic, lively or solemn verse would end at the start of your turn, spend 20 MP: it lasts until the start of your next turn instead (ending early if you sing again).

Through Vast Collection, create a temporary working copy of any Artifact you have seen or heard of. The GM sets the duration — moments for something like the Final Feather, days for something lesser. Strong, and safe precisely because the GM holds the clock. No amendment.
heroic_skills.requirements: Antiquarian (Dungeoneer) or Engineer (Tinkerer) mastery + Vast Collection

heroic_skills.summary: After an enemy deals damage to you while you are in Crisis: spend 10 MP to apply Bone Crusher's effects to them if they would be a legal target for a melee weapon you are wielding, and/or spend 10 MP to apply Warning Shot's effects if they would be a legal target for a ranged weapon you are wielding.

You make contact with an unknown Arcanum and bind it to your soul — designed with the rest of the group, and while you live no one else in your world can bind it. Once per scene while merged, use an action and spend 2 Fabula Points to trigger that Arcanum's dismiss effect without dismissing them; this does not trigger the Arcane Circle Skill. Rewritten by the variant Arcanist. Level-up only.

Ripples' free attack may instead be a free non-"hex" invocation you have access to, ignoring its MP cost — same single target, damage retyped to the ally's, and all hexes on the target still end when it resolves.

When you perform a Ritual outside a conflict scene with a total cost of 60 MP or lower, stop immediately before the Magic Check and store the effect in a Ritual seal on a surface you can touch. Name a condition — anything from "when I enter Crisis" to "as soon as I snap my fingers". When it is met the seal vanishes, the Ritual fires at the seal's location, and you make the Magic Check and resolve it even if you are unconscious or not present. One seal at a time; dying or making a new seal destroys the old one. This campaign's Symbolist has no Rituals — Mirage is dead — so the only route is the benefit-pool Ritualism pick with a named discipline. Legal, and a real build, but a payoff you buy outside the class.
heroic_skills.requirements: Symbolist mastery (and, in practice, the Ritualism benefit-pool pick)

heroic_skills.summary: Permanently increase your Crisis score by half your level; while genuinely that low — gated on actual current HP, not inflated Crisis status — your damage ignores Resistances.

While your current HP are below maximum: action + 20 MP deals dark damage equal to (10 + half the gap between maximum and current HP) to one enemy — the type cannot change, and it bypasses nothing: not Absorption, not Immunity, not Resistance. ✎ A house cut, re-cut on balance 15 Aug 2026 — the printed Absorption and Immunity clauses stay struck on their own merits, not on the retired doctrine. A nearly-dead Blackguard still deals enormous damage.

When visible allies drop to 0 HP, if your garden holds a magiseed and 2+ Growth sections are full: remove the seed, erase the clock, and one of them is reduced to exactly 1 HP instead. And whenever a seed leaves your garden with 3+ sections full, recover 20 MP.

At the start of your turn in a conflict, with no martial armor equipped, spend 1 Fabula Point to perform up to three different dances you know, in any order, paying no MP. If you do, you cannot perform dances in any way until the end of your next turn. Three dances for one Fabula Point and a turn and a half of silence afterwards — Banshee into Nightmare into Satyr, in one go.

A High Speed free attack with a bow, spear or thrown weapon deals extra damage equal to (your Skill Level in High Speed × 5). And when you attack one or more creatures with a bow, spear or thrown weapon, those creatures cannot perform free attacks until the end of the current turn.
heroic_skills.requirements: Rogue, Sharpshooter, Prizefighter (Weaponmaster) or Bounty Hunter mastery + High Speed

heroic_skills.summary: When you use Runic Spell you may cast a second spell as a runic spell, naming a separate, distinct trigger different from the first. The second spell's total HP and/or MP cost must be equal to or lower than the first's.
heroic_skills.requirements: Entropist, Reaper (Necromancer) or Sin-Eater (Witch) mastery + Runic Spell

heroic_skills.summary: Potions and delicacies you create, and spells you cast, may take a creature's HP and MP above their maximums, to a ceiling of 150% of each score. At the end of each scene anything still above maximum drops back to maximum. ✎ The printed requirement also lists Merchant, which is cut — three routes, not four.
heroic_skills.requirements: Cook (Gourmet), Archivist (Loremaster) or Engineer (Tinkerer) mastery (the Merchant route is cut)

heroic_skills.summary: Action + 10 MP: airborne — your melee attacks reach the unreachable, and other creatures cannot see you ( so cannot read your Tell; case-by-case, as ruled). At your turn's start you descend: Soaring Strike costs no MP that turn, and with a spear it gains multi (2) and +10 damage. Printed: no two PCs may both hold it. The flight ruling of 7 Aug applies: going up where anyone can see you ticks the Miasma Clock by 1.
heroic_skills.requirements: The Soaring Strike spell (Core p. 189); no two PCs may both acquire it

heroic_skills.summary: On acquisition, choose three different tastes and three different effects from the printed list — 20 dark or light damage (30 at level 30+), a damage-type lock, stripping every Scene-duration spell, a forced-target clause, enraged, poisoned, 30 HP and 30 MP (40/40 at 30+), one status of the target's choice, the dazed/enraged/shaken cleanse, or the poisoned/slow/weak cleanse. When you create a delicacy with exactly 3 ingredients during a conflict and each matches a different one of your chosen tastes, ignore the delicacy's normal effects and apply one, two or all three of yours instead. This is the answer to the randomness, and the class's only route to dark and light damage — expect it to be the mastery pick.

Spend 1 Fabula Point on top of the usual MP cost to enact a law of your own design instead of a printed one; the GM adjudicates the wording. The best thing in the class for this campaign, because it converts a conflict into an objective — and a Magistrate who declares the ground rules pairs with an Antiquarian who works them, since Objective actions fill Pressure Clocks.

Learn two therioforms; at each rest, stabilize up to two you know — never polypoda, at most one of arpaktida/dynamotheria/tachytheria. Stabilized forms persist between scenes and through Guard; elemental forms add their matching Resistance. The one exception to flight-is-temporary — and by the worn-Guise rule it functions unmasked only.

After you perform an invocation during a conflict, you and up to one ally you can see each increase one Attribute's die size by one, to a maximum of d12, until the end of the scene or until you use this again. The Attribute follows the wellspring: air → Insight, earth → any Attribute of your choice, fire → Dexterity, lightning → Might, water → Willpower. Held by the standing rulings rather than a bespoke one: die raises never stack and d12 is the ceiling everywhere, and Guise bonuses sit outside p.266's two-effect cap — so this is one raise, on a class ability, with the mask's +3 not counted against it. Still the only skill in the class that hands a scene-long raise to somebody else; watch it in play.

You acquire a following who define their way of life by you and their worship — often metaphorical — of you. With the rest of the group, design a level 10 humanoid, then halve its maximum HP and MP; that becomes a permanent Entourage Member.

✎ Printed, this let you choose Trick or Treat's effect instead of rolling. In Unmasked you roll twice and choose which result to apply. The printed version turns the skill into 2 IP for a guaranteed 40 damage, no roll, no defence, at will — it deletes the only thing that made the class distinct. Rolling twice keeps the promise (the trick usually lands the way you wanted) and keeps the gamble (it can still come up two bad results).
heroic_skills.requirements: Confidence Man mastery + Trick or Treat — "You must have mastered this class and know Trick or Treat Skill" (AzureProject Trickster doc p.3, verified 10 Aug 2026)

heroic_skills.summary: Ranged attacks with thrown weapons, with no martial armor and no shields equipped, earn 1 Momentum Point to a maximum of 5, and your thrown attacks deal extra damage equal to your current Momentum. When a creature hits you with an attack against Defense you must spend all your Momentum and add an equal amount to your Defense against that attack — which can turn the hit into a miss. Momentum is lost at the end of each scene, or the moment you equip a shield or martial armor. A defence you cannot decline.

After you use Bishop's Edict or King's Castle, if you are in Crisis, every enemy in the scene loses 10 Hit Points — 20 at level 20+, 30 at level 40+. Note the vector: HP loss, not damage. No Affinities, no Resistances, no Defense. The Crisis gate is the whole cost, and a Captain who is winning never gets to use it.

Tactical Leverage grants an ally two benefits instead of one. With a shield equipped you may also forgo the benefits of covering them to have them treated as flying until the end of their next turn, provided they meet the conditions for flying. The flying clause stands, ruled 7 Aug: flight is real in 1892, and using it in public view ticks the Miasma Clock by 1. A shield-boosted vault over a gap or onto a roof costs nothing; doing it in the street is the sort of thing people talk about.
heroic_skills.requirements: Captain (Commander), Guardian or Batman (Squire) mastery + Tactical Leverage

heroic_skills.summary: Spend 20 MP to ignore Symbolism's IP cost for a conflict.
heroic_skills.requirements: Arcanist, Symbolist or Spiritist mastery + Symbolism (the Merchant route is cut)

heroic_skills.summary: Your equipped brawling and dagger weapons also count as arcane. Action: single-target free attack with an arcane weapon, High Roll 0, then a rider resolves (see print).

While you are in Crisis, you are flying: your melee attacks can target flying creatures, and melee cannot reach you unless the attacker flies or can otherwise reach flying targets. Suspended whenever you cannot fly freely — inside a vehicle built for human-sized creatures, in a narrow corridor — and lost until the start of your next turn if you suffer air, earth or light damage in a conflict. Flight in public view ticks the Miasma Clock by 1; used in a cellar, in the works, or at night with nobody watching, it costs nothing. Not the cut Skilled Sinning: two heroics in that book share the name, the Sinner's dies with its class, and this is the other one. The rename ends the collision.
heroic_skills.requirements: Sensitive (Esper), Elementalist, Entropist or Spiritist mastery

heroic_skills.summary: Choose one damage type from air, bolt, dark, earth, fire, ice, light or poison. When you deal air, earth, fire or ice damage you gain a spirit orb of that type — one of each at a time, vanishing at the end of the scene. Holding one of each grants a unique spell: 50 HP, special target, instantaneous — every enemy you can see suffers 10 earth, then 10 ice, then 10 fire, then 10 air, then (10 + the total Inferiority, Mistrust and Hatred emotions among your Bonds) of your chosen type. On casting, your orbs vanish and you must replace one Bond's emotion of Admiration, Affection or Loyalty with Inferiority, Mistrust or Hatred; if you do not, the spell has no effect.
heroic_skills.requirements: Elementalist, Entropist, Spiritist or Sin-Eater (Witch) mastery

heroic_skills.summary: ✎(printed: Create Phantasm: Numen) Spend 50 MP to create a fourth Phantasm outside the three-Phantasm limit. Only one at a time, and if you have four Phantasms one must be it. It takes its own turn with a single action, before or after yours, for 3 turns, then shatters; it has your Hit Points; enemies can target it and your allies cannot; and no Skill or Command spell may use it. Its attack deals (HR + 14), rising to (HR + 18) at 20+ and (HR + 20) at 40+, at your equipped weapon's range. Choose an essence at each casting to fix its damage type — physical, light or dark. Its damage ignores Immunities and Resistances, as printed. ⚠ The printed essence names (Ravana, Asura, Diablos) do not survive 1892 — they are simply a physical apparition, a bright one and a dark one. ⚠ The source prints no Requirements line; Illusionist mastery is an inference, not a quotation.
heroic_skills.requirements: ⚠ No Requirements line printed — Illusionist mastery inferred, in line with every other class heroic

heroic_skills.summary: While you are in Crisis, after you sing a verse at medium or high volume, immediately sing another verse in the same key but with a different tone as a free action, paying no MP. Not in the same turn as Vibrato.

With a transforming custom weapon equipped whose forms are one melee and one ranged: use Bone Crusher and Counterattack with its ranged form, and Crossfire and Warning Shot with its melee form — never Bone Crusher and Warning Shot on the same attack. After you use Bone Crusher or Warning Shot with a melee weapon, each enemy hit becomes ruptured until the end of the scene; when a ruptured enemy takes damage from anything other than a melee attack, they suffer 5 extra damage and stop being ruptured. Ruptured is a primed condition on the Anatomist's reeling precedent — not a seventh status, so no cleanse removes it, and it clears the moment it pays. It is private to this heroic: it never shares a trigger or a payout with reeling or broken. Requires the class only, not mastery, as printed: the source says "even if you have not mastered them" and means it.
heroic_skills.requirements: The Sharpshooter and/or Prizefighter (Weaponmaster) Class — acquired, not mastered, as printed

heroic_skills.summary: While a Villain is present and/or you are in the Panoply, treat your Bond strengths as 1 higher. After a GM scene showing danger to a place or to non-Villain NPCs, spend 1 Fabula Point to declare your character felt it, and knows where.
heroic_skills.requirements: Sensitive (Esper), Penny Knight or Symbolist mastery

heroic_skills.summary: At the start of your turn in a conflict, choose one: reveal one of a creature's Traits, or name a damage type and reveal its Affinity. Inherits the pressure-point clause — one free reveal per turn, forever. The discovery half of the game getting its capstone.

Hand a debt you owe from Fey's Debt to another willing character. You cannot use the skill again until that debt has been fulfilled. No cost, no action type, at will — and explicitly your own Fey's Debt debts only; an NPC's debt or an obligation incurred any other way does not qualify. The self-lock is the balance: one outstanding transfer at a time, and it stays locked until somebody else clears your obligation.
Secretly assign a damage type, a status and an action to a trap; it springs when the enemy takes that action. The prediction mechanic — pairs with Prophetic Defender and Battlefield Investigator.
When a travel or encounter roll produces a Danger, spend 1 Fabula Point to make a Discovery at the same time — interwoven with the Danger or one after the other, the GM chooses.
heroic_skills.requirements: Antiquarian (Dungeoneer) or Traveller (Wayfarer) mastery + Treasure Hunter and Treasure Magnet

heroic_skills.summary: When you make a weapon attack, you may instead disguise it as a feint and prepare a Secret Action with the trigger: "When the target next makes an attack roll." When triggered, you strike first, dealing 5 extra damage with your weapon attack. If the attack hits, the target suffers a -2 penalty to their next check. The word "instead" is why this costs your action. (AzureProject Trickster doc p.3, verified 10 Aug 2026 — the audit had held one clause of this.)
heroic_skills.requirements: Confidence Man mastery — "You must have mastered this class" (AzureProject Trickster doc p.3, verified 10 Aug 2026)

heroic_skills.summary: With a one-handed melee dagger or sword in each normal hand slot, you may treat your armor slot as a second off-hand slot, usable only for another one-handed dagger or sword. With three equipped, the Attack action attacks once with each; two-weapon rules apply to all three (each loses the multi property and cannot gain it, and each treats High Roll as 0). Monkey Grip does not help. It spends the armor slot — check against the Innate Guise's ordinary-purchased-armor allowance before anyone builds around it.
When you willingly dismiss an Arcanum not summoned this same turn: choose dark, light or physical — you and every visible ally gain Resistance to it until your next turn.

When Arming Maneuver both makes a free attack with a weapon you just equipped and swaps equipment with an ally, that ally may attack alongside you. Both attacks treat High Roll as 0 and both deal extra damage equal to your Skill Level in Arming Maneuver. You generate an opportunity if any two of the four dice rolled show 6 or higher and match.
heroic_skills.requirements: Sharpshooter, Batman (Squire) or Prizefighter (Weaponmaster) mastery + Arming Maneuver

heroic_skills.summary: Biophagy / Life Transference healing +10, and the target gains temporary immunity to one of poisoned/slow/weak, or temporary Resistance to physical and poison, until your next turn.

Charging Cavalry's ally may forgo the free attack for a free Equipment, Hinder or Study — or a free Spell action casting a spell of 20 MP or less (still paid; offensive casts get +your SL in Charging Cavalry to the Check, High Roll 0).
When you attack you may forego the Weapon Mastery bonus; if you do, the attack deals extra damage equal to (that bonus + your Skill Level in Surgical Slices).
heroic_skills.requirements: Butcher, Sharpshooter or Prizefighter (Weaponmaster) mastery + Surgical Slices + Melee Weapon Mastery or Ranged Weapon Mastery

heroic_skills.summary: +5 to Accuracy and Magic Checks against targets that include an enemy in Crisis. After you defeat one or more enemies: recover from all statuses, then a single-target free attack at +5 damage or a free offensive spell of 10 MP or less, unpaid. Once per conflict per trigger window.
heroic_skills.requirements: Entropist or Rogue mastery + High Speed or Stolen Time

heroic_skills.summary: On your turn, after you apply a gift's effects: every ally present recovers (1 + filled Brainwave sections) MP — doubled for your focus. Stacks with Reassuring Presence.
Sing Chanter verses through a device without having taken Magichant. Requires magispheres — the Superior Magitech tier of Gadgets.

When you hit with a ranged attack, spend 10 MP to leave a weak point. The next time any creature hits that same target this scene, they may spend 10 MP to deal 15 extra damage and inflict one status of their choice from dazed, shaken, slow or weak. The damage rises to 25 at level 40+.

Once during each of your turns, choose one: while you are in Crisis with Theriomorphosis active, before or after an action, replace one active therioform with another you have learned; or, when you use Genoclepsis in Crisis with Theriomorphosis active, replace one active therioform with one of the GM's choices instead of activating Theriomorphosis. You may end up carrying a mixture of your own forms and the GM's. This does not nest a transformation inside a transformation — it rearranges the one you are already in, which is why the Mutant's Innate-only rule is untouched. By the worn-Guise rule it functions unmasked only.

Grants a Moon wellspring on odd rounds and a Sun wellspring on even ones, in addition to the scene's own. These wellsprings can never be marked miasmatic — they are conjured, not drawn from anybody's ground.

Action during a conflict: a free attack with an equipped two-handed ranged thrown custom weapon, gaining multi (2) — still enhanceable to 3 by Barrage. If it hits, you may send the weapon spinning. At the start of your turn, if it is still spinning, it stops and you choose up to two: every enemy you can see loses 5 HP; or loses 5 MP; or suffers slow; or fill or erase 1 section of a Clock. HP and MP losses rise to 10 at level 30+. It stops spinning at once if you unequip it, attack with it again, or the scene ends. The Clock option is conflict Clocks only, settled in the Clock-effects sweep.

After a haunting verse, or a successful Opposed Check for Condemn: choose one enemy among the targets and one status it suffers. It is bewitched until your next turn or until it sheds that status — and must include you among its attack and offensive-spell targets, if able.
An ally's damage becomes light and ignores Resistances.
